searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['categories'] = array( '1' => 'News', '2' => 'Events & Seminars', );   Template <select name="category"> <option value="">All</option> {{ options source=$page.categories selected=$in.category }} </select>   Output (request ?category=2) <select name="category"> <option value="">All</option> <option value='1'>News</option><option value='2' selected>Events &amp; Seminars</option> </select>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ include '/path/to/template' }}   Renders another template at this place, with the same variables. Variables the included template assigns do not come back to the including one.  {{ include head '/path/to/template' }} {{ head }} {{ include foot '/path/to/template' }} {{ foot }}   {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} do not output anything where they are written. They queue a template that is rendered later where the layout writes {{ head }} (in <head>) or {{ foot }} (before </body>). A page uses them to add its own CSS or JavaScript to the shared layout. When several templates queue partials (a page and the layouts it transcludes), the partials of the outer layouts come first.  {{ include html '/data/html/banner.html' }}   {{ include html }} includes a file under the document root (htdocs/) with PHP's include. The path starts with / and has its extension. It is not a template: {{ }} tags in it are not compiled.

searchDocs.title: Paths​
searchDocs.content: Template paths have no .tpl extension.A path starting with / is relative to the template root (site/template/, then core/template/). Prefer it: it works the same from any directory.A path without / is relative to the directory of the template that contains the tag (./parts/card, ../include/head/news). For include head / include foot, it stays relative to the template that queued it.A missing target throws Fegg\Template\TemplateException (HTTP 500). ./fegg-cli template:lint reports missing targets before you deploy (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: include​
searchDocs.content: site/template/parts/card.tpl <div class="c-card">{{ $page.title }}</div>   site/template/news/detail.tpl <p>Before</p> {{ include '/parts/card' }}   Output <p>Before</p> <div class="c-card">Hello</div>

searchDocs.title: include head / include foot​
searchDocs.content: site/template/include/head/about.tpl <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ base }}/data/css/about.css">   site/template/include/foot/about.tpl <script src="{{ base }}/data/js/about.js"></script>   site/template/about.tpl {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ include head '/include/head/about' }} {{ include foot '/include/foot/about' }} {{ section contents }} <p>About us</p> {{ end section contents }}   site/template/template/siteframe.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>{{ $site.title }}</title> {{ head }} </head> <body> {{ section contents }} {{ end section contents }} {{ foot }} </body> </html>   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Example Inc.</title> <link rel="stylesheet" href="/data/css/about.css"> </head> <body> <p>About us</p> <script src="/data/js/about.js"></script> </body> </html>   メモ Write {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} at the top level of the template, not inside a {{ section }}: a section runs as a function, so a partial queued inside it is lost.

searchDocs.title: foreach​
searchDocs.content: {{ foreach $array as $key => $value }} {{ end foreach }} {{ foreach $array as $value }} {{ end }}   Repeats the block for every element of an array, like PHP's foreach. The key is optional. The block is closed by {{ end foreach }} or simply {{ end }}.  When the array is not set, the block is skipped without a warning.$foreachIndex counts the iterations from 0. In nested loops, the inner loop has its own $foreachIndex and the outer value is restored when the inner loop ends. After a loop, $foreachIndex holds the number of iterations.The key and value variables live in the same namespace as $page, $site …: {{ foreach $list as $page }} overwrites $page. Pick other names.

searchDocs.title: loop​
searchDocs.content: {{ loop $i = 1 to 10 }} {{ end }}   Counts from the first bound to the second, both included: {{ loop $i = 1 to 10 }} is for ($i = 1; $i <= 10; $i++). Each bound is a number or a variable ($page.pager.last_page), not an expression. A bound that is not set reads as null. Close the block with {{ end }}.

searchDocs.title: foreach​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['list'] = array('foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux');   Template <ul> {{ foreach $page.list as $key => $value }} <li>{{ $foreachIndex }} : {{ $key }} => {{ $value }}</li> {{ end foreach }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>0 : foo => bar</li> <li>1 : baz => qux</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: Nested foreach​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['rows'] = array(array('a', 'b'), array('c', 'd', 'e'));   Template {{ foreach $page.rows as $row }}[{{ foreach $row as $cell }}{{ $cell }}{{ end }}:{{ $foreachIndex }}]{{ end }}   Output [ab:0][cde:1]

searchDocs.title: loop​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['max'] = 5;   Template <ul> {{ loop $i = 1 to $page.max }} <li>{{ $i }}</li> {{ end }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>1</li> <li>2</li> <li>3</li> <li>4</li> <li>5</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {-{ ... }-} {--{ ... }--}   Fegg treats every {{ ... }} as a tag. To output literal double braces, for example a Vue or Handlebars template inside the page, or copy that contains them, write {-{ for {{ and }-} for }}. The text between them is not compiled.  {-{ also removes the spaces directly before it, and }-} the spaces directly after it (a {-{ x }-} b outputs a{{ x }}b). {--{ and }--} work the same but remove all whitespace there, newlines included.  Single braces ({, }) in HTML, CSS and JavaScript need nothing special.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <div id="app"> <p>{-{ message }-}</p> </div> <script> Vue.createApp({ data() { return { message: 'Hello' }; } }).mount('#app'); </script>   Output <div id="app"> <p>{{ message }}</p> </div> <script> Vue.createApp({ data() { return { message: 'Hello' }; } }).mount('#app'); </script>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ base }} {{ base_url }} {{ current_url }}   Tag	Output	Example{{ base }}	URL path of the site root, without a trailing slash. Empty when the site is at the document root	(empty), /sub {{ base_url }}	Scheme, host (and port) plus {{ base }}: the absolute URL of the site root	https://example.com, https://example.com/sub {{ current_url }}	Absolute URL of the current request, including the query string	https://example.com/news/?p=2  All three are HTML-escaped.  Start every link and asset path with {{ base }}/, so the site keeps working when it is installed in a subdirectory. Use {{ base_url }} and {{ current_url }} where an absolute URL is required (canonical, OGP).

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ base }}/data/css/style.css"> <a href="{{ base }}/news/">News</a> <img src="{{ base }}/data/img/common/pc/logo.png" alt=""> <link rel="canonical" href="{{ current_url }}"> <meta property="og:image" content="{{ base_url }}/data/img/ogp.png">   Output (site at https://example.com/, page /news/?p=2) <link rel="stylesheet" href="/data/css/style.css"> <a href="/news/">News</a> <img src="/data/img/common/pc/logo.png" alt=""> <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/news/?p=2"> <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/data/img/ogp.png">

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ $var }} {{ $var.key.sub }} {{ $var|modifier }}   {{ $var }} outputs a variable. Array elements are separated with a period: $var.key.sub is $var['key']['sub']. Numeric keys and keys that are PHP keywords work too ($rows.0.name, $item.new, $site.default). Square brackets take an expression as the key: $page.data[$id], $map[$key].name.  Values from the controller are set in $this->page and read as $page in the template. The other variables available in a page are listed in Application::fetchPage.  The output is escaped with htmlspecialchars (ENT_QUOTES), which is right for HTML text and quoted attribute values. Other places (URLs, JavaScript) need a modifier: see Security. To output trusted HTML as it is, use the noescape modifier (see Modifiers).  Nothing is output (and no error is raised) when the variable is not set, or when it is an array and no modifier is applied. Modifiers receive arrays, so {{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }} and {{ $items|feggJs|noescape }} work; a chain whose result is still an array outputs nothing.  Inside a tag, $a.b is always array access. To concatenate strings in an expression (if, assign …), write the PHP operator with spaces: $a . $b.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['title'] = 'Hello'; $this->page['rows'] = array( array('name' => 'first'), ); $this->displayPage('template');   Template {{ $page.title }} {{ $page.rows.0.name }} {{ $page.missing }}   Output Hello first

searchDocs.title: Escaping and noescape​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['foo'] = '<p>bar</p>';   Template {{ $page.foo }} {{ $page.foo|noescape }}   Output &lt;p&gt;bar&lt;/p&gt; <p>bar</p>   警告 Use noescape only for HTML you trust (CMS rich text written by administrators, messages from your own config). Never use it on request parameters ($in) or other user input.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ transclude '/path/to/layout' }} {{ section name }} {{ end section name }}   {{ transclude }} makes the template inherit a layout (the parent template). The parent declares named {{ section }} blocks; the child fills them, and the parent prints each one where it is declared.  In the parent, a section is a placeholder. Its content is the default, printed when the child does not define the section.In the child, a section defines the content. The section name must match the parent's.Inheritance works through any number of levels: a child can fill a section declared by its parent or by any layout further up.A template has one {{ transclude }}. Paths follow the include rules: prefer /-rooted paths such as '/template/siteframe'. A missing parent throws Fegg\Template\TemplateException with the line of the tag.Close a section with {{ end section name }} (recommended) or {{ end section }}.  Things to know:  Text outside any {{ section }} in a child template is output before the parent layout. Keep everything inside sections (fegg-cli template:lint warns about stray text).A section runs as a function. {{ assign }}, {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} written inside it only affect that section. Put them at the top level of the template, next to {{ transclude }}.A section the parent does not declare is printed where the child defines it.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: site/template/template/siteframe.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>{{ $site.title }}</title> </head> <body> <main> {{ section contents }} <p>Default content</p> {{ end section contents }} </main> </body> </html>   site/template/index.tpl {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ section contents }} <p>This is the index content.</p> {{ end section contents }}   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Example Inc.</title> </head> <body> <main> <p>This is the index content.</p> </main> </body> </html>

searchDocs.title: Multiple levels​
searchDocs.content: site/template/base.tpl <html> <body> {{ section header }}<header>Default header</header>{{ end section header }} {{ section body }}{{ end section body }} </body> </html>   site/template/layout/two_columns.tpl {{ transclude '/base' }} {{ section body }} <div class="l-columns"> <aside>Menu</aside> <div class="l-columns__main"> {{ section main }}{{ end section main }} </div> </div> {{ end section body }}   site/template/news/detail.tpl {{ transclude '/layout/two_columns' }} {{ section header }}<header>News</header>{{ end section header }} {{ section main }} <p>This is the news content.</p> {{ end section main }}   Output (whitespace simplified) <html> <body> <header>News</header> <div class="l-columns"> <aside>Menu</aside> <div class="l-columns__main"> <p>This is the news content.</p> </div> </div> </body> </html>   news/detail fills header, which is declared two levels up in base, and main, which is declared by its direct parent.

searchDocs.title: Basic settings​
searchDocs.content: The defaults are in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/settings.php. Do not edit that file (it is replaced on update). Put the values for your project in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php.  The core file is loaded first, then the site file. Only the keys the site file sets are changed, so write one key per line and never reassign the whole array ($settings = array(...) would drop the defaults).  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // Run mode 1: running, empty: under maintenance $settings['run_mode'] = '1'; // Maintenance page URL $settings['maintenance_page_url'] = ''; // Developer IP addresses (multiple allowed). Error details only outside production (FEGG_ENV) $settings['developer_ip'] = array('192.168.65.1', '203.0.113.10'); // Basic authentication scope (0: none, 1: whole site, 2: partial) #$settings['basic_auth_scope'] = 0; #$settings['basic_auth_user'] = ''; #$settings['basic_auth_password'] = ''; // HSTS, once the whole site is served over HTTPS #$settings['hsts'] = 'max-age=31536000';   Per-server values and secrets (the environment, database passwords, API keys) do not belong here: see Environments and secrets.  Key	Default	Remarksrun_mode	'1'	'1': running. Empty: under maintenance. During maintenance every request that does not come from developer_ip is redirected to maintenance_page_url, or gets a short maintenance message when it is empty. maintenance_page_url	''	Redirect target during maintenance developer_ip	array()	Addresses that can see error details outside production (see Developer mode) and that bypass maintenance timezone	''	Time zone of the application, set once at startup. '': FEGG_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE (Asia/Tokyo) log_level	''	Lowest level written to the application log (debug, info, notice, warning, error ...). '': warning in production, debug elsewhere. See Logging and errors log_retention_days	30	Days to keep the application log files (0: keep all) mail	array('transport' => 'sendmail')	Outgoing mail of Fegg\Tool\Mail. For SMTP see Mail security_headers	array()	Changes the default security headers: 'Header-Name' => 'value', '' removes one. See Security hsts	''	Strict-Transport-Security value sent on HTTPS responses, e.g. 'max-age=31536000'. '': not sent csp	''	Content-Security-Policy value. '': not sent csp_report_only	false	true: send the policy as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only (reports only, blocks nothing) default_language	not set	Language code used when none is detected, e.g. 'ja'. Only for multilingual sites support_language	not set	Supported language codes, e.g. array('ja', 'en'). Only for multilingual sites basic_auth_scope	0	0: no Basic authentication. 1: every page rendered by Fegg. 2: only where the controller calls $this->basicAuth() basic_auth_user	''	Basic authentication user basic_auth_password	''	Basic authentication password (compared with hash_equals()) basic_auth_message	not set	Realm shown in the browser's login dialog basic_auth_error_message	not set	Text sent with the 401 response when the login fails (default Authorization Required) template_dir	site/template, core/template	Template directories, searched in this order template_ext	'tpl'	Template file extension template_cache_dir	site/data/cache/template	Compiled template cache global_config_dir	''	Optional directory searched by loadConfig() before site/config/. End it with /  Read a setting from a controller with $this->getSetting().

searchDocs.title: Environments and secrets​
searchDocs.content: Values that differ per server (the environment, the database, API keys, passwords) are not written in settings.php or any other committed file. They are read with feggEnv():  $secret = feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''); // feggEnv(string $name, mixed $default = null)   feggEnv() returns the first of:  the environment variable with that name (SetEnv in Apache, fastcgi_param in nginx, Docker environment ...),the key in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php,the key in the committed environment file htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env/<name>.php chosen for this server by its path (see Test servers deployed with git pull),$default.  SetEnv reaches only the web. fegg-cli (and a fegg-cli migration run after a deploy) sees only its own shell's environment and the files, so keep database settings in a file when the server runs fegg-cli.  env.php returns a PHP array. It is in .gitignore and is created on each server by copying site/config/env.php.dist:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; return array( // production | staging | development 'FEGG_ENV' => 'development', // Database. Default: SQLite file in site/data/db/db.db // 'FEGG_DB_DSN' => 'mysql:host=127.0.0.1;port=3306;dbname=example;charset=utf8mb4', // 'FEGG_DB_USER' => '', // 'FEGG_DB_PASSWORD' => '', // Contact form spam protection 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY' => '', 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET' => '', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY' => '', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET' => '', );   Name	Used forFEGG_ENV	production (default, also for unknown values), staging or development. Available as the constant FEGG_ENV FEGG_DB_DSN, FEGG_DB_USER, FEGG_DB_PASSWORD, FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN	Database connection (see Database) FEGG_DB_PATH	SQLite file path, when FEGG_DB_DSN is not set FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY, FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET, FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET	Contact form spam protection (see Captcha) FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD (FEGG_SMTP_HOST, FEGG_SMTP_USERNAME)	SMTP sending (see Mail) FEGG_LOG_DIR	Directory of the application log instead of site/data/log FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SCORE_THRESHOLD	reCAPTCHA score needed (default 0.5; 1.0 rejects every form, to check the error message) FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN, FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_NAME, FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH (or FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD)	First CMS user, created by fegg-cli migration FEGG_ENV_NAME	Environment variable only: chooses site/config/env/<name>.php instead of paths.php  Add your own keys the same way and read them with feggEnv('NAME', $default).  警告 A site without env.php and without a matching environment file runs as production. On your machine, create env.php with 'FEGG_ENV' => 'development'. Otherwise developers do not see error details there. Test servers on the LionHeart develop server run as staging without any file of their own (next section).  FEGG_ENV decides:  whether developer mode is possible (not in production),whether the contact form sends the administrator mail to the test address (outside production),the default log_level (warning in production, debug elsewhere),the Fegg 4 constant FEGG_TEST_ENVIRONMENT, which is true outside production. It no longer looks at the host name.

searchDocs.title: Test servers deployed with git pull​
searchDocs.content: On the LionHeart develop server (http://p83.<project>.develop.lionheart.co.jp/, project directory /var/www/vhosts/<project>/p83) a deploy is git pull followed by fegg-cli migration. Nothing can be placed on the server by hand, so the test server's settings are committed:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env/paths.php return array( // project root pattern (fnmatch; * and ? do not cross /) => environment file name '/var/www/vhosts/*/p[0-9]*' => 'staging', );   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env/staging.php return array( 'FEGG_ENV' => 'staging', // first CMS user, created by fegg-cli migration (see below) 'FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN' => 'admin', 'FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH' => '$2y$10$...', // ./fegg-cli user:hash // Turnstile test keys: always pass (2x00000000000000000000AB / 2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA always fail) 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY' => '1x00000000000000000000AA', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET' => '1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA', );   Both files come with the skeleton. The project root (the directory of fegg-cli) is matched against paths.php; the first match chooses site/config/env/<name>.php. Any other path (production, your machine) does not match and behaves as before.  Why the path: the host name of a request is chosen by the client. Matching it would let a request to production with Host: x.develop.lionheart.co.jp switch production to the test settings (test captcha keys that always pass, the test administrator). The path is set by the server, and fegg-cli sees the same path as the web.Check it: the first line of fegg-cli migration in the deploy log names the environment and its file, e.g. Environment: staging (site/config/env/staging.php, /var/www/vhosts/*/p[0-9]*) / DB: sqlite:....First CMS user: fegg-cli migration creates FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN when no row with that login exists, deleted rows included. It never changes an existing user, so it is safe on every deploy: a password changed in the CMS stays, and a deleted user does not come back. Commit the hash (./fegg-cli user:hash), not the password, and change the password after the first login.Captcha: the Turnstile test keys need no host name registration. reCAPTCHA v3 has no test keys: use a key registered for develop.lionheart.co.jp. 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SCORE_THRESHOLD' => '1.0' shows the rejection.  警告 Everyone who can read the repository can read these files. Put only values made for the test server there, never production keys or passwords. env.php on a server and environment variables still win over them.

searchDocs.title: Developer mode​
searchDocs.content: Fegg runs in developer mode (the constant FEGG_DEVELOPER is '1') only when both are true:  the request comes from an address in developer_ip, andFEGG_ENV is not production.  In developer mode:  PHP errors are displayed.An uncaught exception shows the message, the file and line, the template line (Template: <file>.tpl:<line>), the stack trace and $this->page. Other visitors get the error page (see Logging and errors). In both cases the error is written to the PHP error log and the application log.The 404 page shows which controller file Fegg tried to load.  On a production server developers see the same error page as everyone; the details are in the logs. developer_ip alone is not a security boundary: behind a proxy or load balancer every request may come from the same address.  Requests from developer_ip also reach the site during maintenance (run_mode empty), in every environment.

searchDocs.title: Database​
searchDocs.content: The connection is set in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database_config.php. The skeleton's file reads it from feggEnv(), so the file itself is the same on every server. Without settings, it is the SQLite file htdocs/_fegg/site/data/db/db.db.  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php (MySQL) 'FEGG_DB_DSN' => 'mysql:host=127.0.0.1;port=3306;dbname=example;charset=utf8mb4', 'FEGG_DB_USER' => 'example', 'FEGG_DB_PASSWORD' => '...',   Name	RemarksFEGG_DB_DSN	PDO DSN. Default: sqlite: + FEGG_DB_PATH FEGG_DB_USER, FEGG_DB_PASSWORD	User and password (MySQL) FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN	Read-only replica. Default: the same as the master FEGG_DB_PATH	SQLite file. Default site/data/db/db.db. As an environment variable it wins over FEGG_DB_DSN in env.php (the test suite uses it)  master is used for writes and slave for reads. With one database both point to the same DSN.If the server allows it, put the SQLite file outside the document root with FEGG_DB_PATH (or FEGG_DB_DSN).MySQL / MariaDB are supported, including fegg-cli migration. See Database configuration.  Tables are defined in YAML files (core/config/database/ for the CMS tables, site/config/database/ for the project's tables) and created or changed with ./fegg-cli migration (see fegg-cli). Every table needs the columns valid, created and modified.

searchDocs.title: Other files in site/config/​
searchDocs.content: File	Remarksroute.php	URL routing (see URL) site_info.php	Site title, description, OGP image, picture breakpoints, ... Loaded by the base controller and available in templates as $site category_info.php	Labels for categories and the CMS visibility states. Loaded by the base controller into $this->config['category_info'] cms_menu.php	CMS side menu. Add one block per post type env.php	Per-server settings and secrets, read with feggEnv(). Not committed; copy env.php.dist (see Environments and secrets) database_config.php	Database connection, from feggEnv() (see Database) upload_dir.php	Path and URL of the CMS upload directory (htdocs/up_dir) database/*.yaml	Table definitions for fegg-cli migration define.php	Optional. Project constants, loaded right after the core starts (web and CLI) fegg_update.php	Optional. Repository used by fegg-cli core:update (see Updating the core)  Any other file in site/config/ can be loaded with $this->loadConfig(). A file with the same name as one in core/config/ (for example validation_error_message.php) replaces the core's file.

searchDocs.title: URL and Controller class​
searchDocs.content: Fegg maps URL segments to a controller class, a method and its arguments:  https://example.com/class/method/param1/param2/   Controller class (site/controller/Class.php, first letter in upper case)Method of the controller classArguments for the method  When the method segment is empty, index() is called. When no segment names a controller, the Index controller of that directory is used.  Sub directories of site/controller/ are part of the URL and of the namespace:  URL	File	Called/	site/controller/Index.php	Site\Controller\Index::index() /news/	site/controller/News.php	Site\Controller\News::index() /news/detail/12/	site/controller/News.php	Site\Controller\News::detail('12') /cms/news/edit/3/	site/controller/Cms/News.php	Site\Controller\Cms\News::edit('3') /cms/media/	core/controller/Cms/Media.php (no site class)	Fegg\Controller\Cms\Media::index()  The site (Site\Controller\...) is searched first, then the core (Fegg\Controller\...). A site class with the same name replaces the core's CMS screen (see Controller).Segments are walked from the left; the first one that names a controller file wins over a directory with the same name.Controller and directory names must be valid PHP class names (letters, digits, _). For URLs like /about-us/, use a route.Abstract classes (the base Controller classes) are never called from a URL.If no controller or no method matches, the NotFound controller renders the 404 page.  Arguments are always strings.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: URL https://example.com/post/edit/1/   htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Post.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Post extends Controller { public function edit($id) { echo $id; // Result: 1 } }

searchDocs.title: Trailing slash​
searchDocs.content: URLs without an extension are normalised to end with /. A GET or HEAD request to /news/detail/1 is redirected (301) to /news/detail/1/, keeping the query string. Other methods (POST, ...) are handled in place without a redirect. URLs with an extension (/news/post_1.html) are not changed.  Write links in templates with the trailing slash to avoid the extra redirect.

searchDocs.title: Routing​
searchDocs.content: To use URLs that do not follow the class/method structure, add routes to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php:  $route['from'] = 'to';   The key is the URL (without the leading /) and the value is the class/method/arguments path it is mapped to.  Routes without wildcards are checked first. Then the routes are tried in the order they are written, and the first match wins. Put specific routes above general ones.A route without an extension matches the URL with or without a trailing slash ('contact/' matches /contact and /contact/).When no route matches, the URL itself is used as the path.

searchDocs.title: Wildcards​
searchDocs.content: Wildcard	Matches:num	Digits only ([0-9]+) :any	One segment: any characters except /  Refer to the matched values with $1, $2, ... in the value.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // Handle index.html (in the skeleton by default) $route[':any/index.html'] = '$1/index'; // https://example.com/news/index.html -> Site\Controller\News::index() $route['news/post_:num.html'] = 'news/detail/$1'; // https://example.com/news/post_1.html -> Site\Controller\News::detail('1') $route['item/:any/'] = 'product/item_lookup/$1'; // https://example.com/item/foobar/ -> Site\Controller\Product::item_lookup('foobar') $route['contact/'] = 'contact/index'; $route['contact/confirm.html'] = 'contact/confirm'; // https://example.com/contact/confirm.html -> Site\Controller\Contact::confirm()

searchDocs.title: Static pages​
searchDocs.content: Pages that have no data of their own do not need a controller. Route them to the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page, which renders the template named in the route:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['about/'] = 'page/render/about'; // site/template/about.tpl $route['guide/:any.html'] = 'page/render/guide/$1'; // site/template/guide/*.tpl   Page::render() joins its arguments into the template path. If the template does not exist, it redirects to the top page.

searchDocs.title: Route-only controllers​
searchDocs.content: Page implements the marker interface Fegg\Http\RouteOnly. A controller that implements it is only called through a route in route.php. The default /class/method/arguments mapping skips it, so /page/render/about/ typed in the browser is a 404. This way a visitor cannot choose which template Page renders; only the routes you write can.  Use RouteOnly for your own controllers whose arguments must not come straight from the URL:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Landing.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Http\RouteOnly; class Landing extends Controller implements RouteOnly { public function show($campaign) { $this->page['campaign'] = $campaign; $this->displayPage('landing/' . $campaign); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['campaign/spring/'] = 'landing/show/spring';

searchDocs.title: Escaping by context​
searchDocs.content: {{ $x }} escapes the value with htmlspecialchars (ENT_QUOTES). That is right for HTML text and for quoted attribute values, but not enough in URLs and JavaScript. Use the modifier that matches the place:  Where the value goes	WriteHTML text, quoted attribute values	{{ $x }} <textarea>	{{ $x }} (the browser shows the original text) href / src / action / formaction taking a URL from data	href="{{ $x|feggUrl }}" Inside <script>	var x = {{ $x|feggJs|noescape }}; (no quotes around it) Event attributes (onclick …)	onclick="go({{ $x|feggJs }})" (no quotes around it, keep the escaping) Trusted HTML (CMS rich text, messages from your config)	{{ $x|noescape }}  Always quote attribute values (class="{{ $x }}", not class={{ $x }}).

searchDocs.title: URLs: feggUrl​
searchDocs.content: HTML escaping does not stop a javascript: URL. feggUrl returns # for any URL whose scheme is not http, https, mailto or tel (also when the scheme is disguised with spaces or control characters). Relative URLs are kept.  Template <a href="{{ $page.data.link|feggUrl }}">{{ $page.data.link_label }}</a>   URLs built by the CMS modifiers (getImageUrl, getImageUrlFromDB, getFileUrl, getFileRawUrl) and values from $site (your configuration) do not need it.

searchDocs.title: JavaScript: feggJs​
searchDocs.content: feggJs turns any value (string, number, array, object, null) into a JavaScript literal and encodes <, >, &, ' and ", so the value can neither end the string nor close the <script> element. It writes the quotes itself: do not add your own.  Inside a script element: add noescape <script> var title = {{ $page.title|feggJs|noescape }}; </script>   In an event attribute: keep the escaping <button type="button" onclick="showItem({{ $item.id|feggJs }})">Show</button>   In an attribute, the browser decodes the HTML escaping before it runs the JavaScript, so the normal {{ }} escaping must stay: never add noescape there.  ヒント Arrays and objects work too, so a whole data set can go to a script in one line: Template <script> var items = {{ $page.items|feggJs|noescape }}; // [{"id":1,"title":"..."}, ...] </script>

searchDocs.title: noescape​
searchDocs.content: noescape outputs the value as it is. Use it only for HTML you trust: CMS rich text written by administrators, validation messages from your config, or the result of feggJs inside <script>. Never use it on $in (request parameters) or anything a visitor can type.

searchDocs.title: Templates are code​
searchDocs.content: {{ code }}, conditions, {{ assign }} and modifiers run arbitrary PHP. Treat templates like PHP files:  Only developers may edit templates. Never let site users upload or edit .tpl files.Never build a template name, an include path or a modifier name from user input.A controller that picks the template from its URL arguments must only be reachable through site/config/route.php. Implement Fegg\Http\RouteOnly, as the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page does:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['about/'] = 'page/render/about'; // site/template/about.tpl   /page/render/... typed in the browser is then a 404.

searchDocs.title: What lint checks​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint reports outputs that lack the right modifier:  an output in <script> without feggJs and noescape (scripts with a non-JavaScript type, such as text/template, are skipped);an output in an on... attribute without feggJs, or with noescape;an output at the start of an href, src, action or formaction value without feggUrl (or a CMS URL modifier).  Outputs of $site values are exempt from these checks. See Lint and errors.

searchDocs.title: migration​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli migration   Compares the table definitions in the YAML files with the database (SQLite, or MySQL / MariaDB) and applies the difference (adds tables, columns and indexes).  The core's files (core/config/database/: cms_user, cms_file, cms_image, cms_login_attempt) are read first, then the project's (site/config/database/). A project file with the same name replaces the core's file.Starts with one line naming the environment, its file and the database, e.g. Environment: staging (site/config/env/staging.php, /var/www/vhosts/*/p[0-9]*) / DB: sqlite:... (see Environments and secrets).Prints Fegg-cli migration diff : Not changed when the database already matches, Fegg-cli migration diff : Finished migration after applying changes.Then creates the first CMS user when FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN is set and no row with that login exists (deleted rows included), with FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH (or FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD) and FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_NAME. An existing user is never changed, so this is safe on every deploy. Without a usable password it exits with 1 after the migration.fegg-cli core:update runs it automatically after updating the core.On MySQL the YAML types are mapped to MySQL types and changed tables are altered in place. See Database configuration./cms/migrate/ in the CMS shows the same pending changes and applies them with its "Run migration" button (POST), for servers where you cannot run fegg-cli.  警告 The YAML files are the single source of truth. A table that exists in the database but in no YAML file is dropped, and a column that is not in the YAML is removed with its data. Run it against a copy first when you are not sure that every table is defined.  To create a YAML file from an existing database (for example when you start writing schema files for an old project):  ./fegg-cli migration:db2schema htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/dump.yaml   All tables are written to the one file. Split it into one file per table if you keep it.

searchDocs.title: db:schema​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli db:schema # every table ./fegg-cli db:schema cms_news # one table ./fegg-cli db:schema --json # as JSON   Lists the tables, columns (type, primary key, autoincrement, not null, default) and indexes defined in core/config/database/ and site/config/database/. It reads the YAML files, not the database, so it works without a database. It also warns when a table is missing one of the columns every table needs (valid, created, modified).  Output cms_news (htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/cms_news.yaml) news_id INTEGER primary key, autoincrement, not null visible BOOLEAN category INTEGER title TEXT ... valid BOOLEAN post_date DATETIME created DATETIME modified DATETIME index NEWS_ID unique (news_id)

searchDocs.title: template:lint​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint # every template in site/template and core/template ./fegg-cli template:lint htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl   Checks templates without running them and reports each problem with the .tpl file and line: unknown tags, unclosed blocks or extra {{ end }}, missing include / transclude targets, undefined modifiers, and output in URL attributes, <script> or event attributes that is not escaped for that context.  Output (example) htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:12: unknown modifier "nosuch" (define it in site/functions/*.php) htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:20: {{ $page.data.url }} starts a URL: write {{ $value|feggUrl }} so javascript: URLs are refused NG: 2 problem(s) in 1 template(s)   Prints OK: <n> template(s) when there is nothing to fix. Run it after every template change.

searchDocs.title: CMS users​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli user:create admin "Site administrator" # LOGIN [NAME]; NAME defaults to LOGIN ./fegg-cli user:password admin # set a new password ./fegg-cli user:list # user_id, login and name of every CMS user   Manage the CMS users (table cms_user). user:create and user:password ask for the password twice without showing it. It must have at least 8 characters, and it is stored with password_hash().  The password is never an argument (it would stay in the shell history). To pass it from a script, or where there is no terminal, give it on standard input with --password-stdin:  printf '%s\n' "$CMS_PASSWORD" | ./fegg-cli user:create admin --password-stdin   user:create refuses a login that already exists; use user:password for it.  user:hash prints password_hash() of a password (asked without echo, or --password-stdin) for FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH in a committed environment file.  メモ Fegg 4 created users with the URL /cms/login/create/<name>/<login>/<password>. It is gone in Fegg 5. /cms/register/ still exists in the CMS, but it now needs a CMS login as well as developer mode (a developer_ip address on a server that is not production), so on a production server use fegg-cli.

searchDocs.title: core:status​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli core:status   Prints the core version and compares the core files with core/manifest.json. No changes to core files. means the core is untouched and can be updated. Otherwise it lists the changed files; move those changes to overrides in site/ (see Directory structure).

searchDocs.title: core:update​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli core:update --dry-run # show the difference only ./fegg-cli core:update # update to the latest release tag ./fegg-cli core:update v5.1.0 # update to a given version   Replaces the core with a release of the skeleton repository. See Updating the core for details.  Option	RemarksvX.Y.Z	Version to install. The latest tag when omitted --dry-run	Show what would change without changing anything --force	Overwrite core files that were changed in the project  core:manifest also exists, but it is for skeleton maintainers only (it rebuilds core/manifest.json).

searchDocs.title: doctor​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli doctor # check the .htaccess files on disk ./fegg-cli doctor https://example.com # also request the live site   Without a URL, it checks the files on disk:  htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess denies access,htdocs/.htaccess has the rule for _fegg/,the upload directory htdocs/up_dir/ has its .htaccess that stops uploaded scripts from running (see Security).  With a URL, it also requests files under _fegg/ and the SQLite database (when it is under the document root) on the live site and reports any that can be read.  Prints OK: https://example.com does not expose _fegg/, or NG with the list of problems (exit code 1). You can run it from your local machine against the production URL, which is the easiest check after an FTP upload.  It also prints Warning: lines, without failing, for outdated rules in htdocs/.htaccess: a <IfModule mod_php5.c> block (ignored by PHP 7 and 8), and Apache 2.2 Order / Deny from lines (an HTTP 500 on Apache 2.4 without mod_access_compat; use Require all denied). Compare the file with core/dist/htaccess.dist.

searchDocs.title: install:class​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli install:class <owner>/<repository>   Clones a Fegg library repository (from GitHub, or a full https:// / git: URL) and copies its src/ directory into htdocs/_fegg/site/lib/. This is the Fegg 4 library mechanism: classes in site/lib/ are only loaded through getClass(), which is deprecated in Fegg 5. For new code, put namespaced classes in site/src/ instead.

searchDocs.title: Developer commands in the skeleton​
searchDocs.content: The skeleton repository also has Composer scripts for the test suite and code checks. Composer is only used for development; the application never loads vendor/.  Command	What it doescomposer test	PHPUnit: unit and HTTP integration tests (PHP 7.4 to 8.5). test:unit and test:integration run one suite composer test:mysql	The MySQL tests, against the server given in FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_DSN, FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_USER and FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD (skipped without them) composer analyse	PHPStan (level 5, with a baseline) composer cs:check	PSR-12 check of core/src and the tests (composer cs:fix applies the fixes)  The integration tests run with FEGG_ENV=development and a throwaway SQLite database, so they never touch site/data/db/db.db.

searchDocs.title: Namespaces​
searchDocs.content: Classes are loaded by the core's own autoloader (core/bootstrap/autoload.php). Composer is not required; in the skeleton it is only used for the test suite.  Namespace	DirectoryFegg\	core/src/ Fegg\Controller\	core/controller/ Fegg\Command\	core/bin/ Site\	site/src/ Site\Controller\	site/controller/  Sub directories are namespaces: site/src/Shop/Cart.php is Site\Shop\Cart, site/controller/Cms/News.php is Site\Controller\Cms\News.  Every PHP file under htdocs/_fegg/ must start with defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit;. It stops the file from doing anything when it is requested directly from a URL.

searchDocs.title: Overriding the core​
searchDocs.content: The site is searched first, then the core. This works like a WordPress child theme.  What	How	ExampleTemplates	Put a file at the same path under site/template/	site/template/cms/login.tpl is used instead of core/template/cms/login.tpl Config files	Put a file with the same name in site/config/	site/config/validation_error_message.php replaces the core's messages Settings	Write only the keys you want to change in site/config/settings.php	$settings['developer_ip'] = array(...); CMS screens	Put a class that extends the core controller in site/controller/, with only the methods you change	See Controller CMS menu	Add one block to site/config/cms_menu.php	When you add a post type DB tables	Put a YAML file in site/config/database/ (a file with the same name wins over the core's)	cms_news.yaml

searchDocs.title: Entry files and layout​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/index.php and fegg-cli belong to the project. They only define three paths and then load the core:  htdocs/index.php <?php define('FEGG_HTML_DIR', __DIR__); // document root define('FEGG_CORE_DIR', __DIR__ . '/_fegg/core'); // core define('FEGG_SITE_DIR', __DIR__ . '/_fegg/site'); // site require FEGG_CORE_DIR . '/bootstrap/web.php';   fegg-cli defines the same three constants and requires core/bootstrap/cli.php. Always keep the paths in the two files consistent. Templates for both are in core/dist/.  Layout	Entry fileStandard: htdocs/_fegg/	core/dist/index.php.dist _fegg/ placed next to the document root (outside of it)	core/dist/index.outside-docroot.php.dist The document root has a different name (public_html, etc.)	Keep the standard one. Only fix FEGG_HTML_DIR in fegg-cli Installed in a subdirectory (https://example.com/sub/)	Keep the standard one. The URL base is detected from SCRIPT_NAME

searchDocs.title: Protecting _fegg/​
searchDocs.content: In the standard layout _fegg/ is inside the document root. It is protected by several layers, so that one missing layer is caught by the next:  htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess denies all requests.htdocs/.htaccess returns 403 for /_fegg/, dotfiles and hidden directories (.git/; .well-known/ stays reachable), and denies .db, .sqlite, .yaml, .tpl, .log, .md, .json and .dist files.Every PHP file under _fegg/ and every compiled template starts with defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit;.fegg-cli doctor https://example.com checks over HTTP that nothing under _fegg/ and no database file can be read (see fegg-cli). The CMS dashboard also warns about problems it can detect from the files, such as a missing .htaccess.If the server allows it, put the SQLite database outside the document root (see Settings).  On nginx, where .htaccess is not used, add equivalent rules:  location ~ (^|/)_fegg(/|$) { deny all; } location ~ /\.(?!well-known/) { deny all; } location ~* ^/up_dir/.*\.(php\d?|phtml|phar|pht|cgi|pl|py|sh)$ { deny all; } location ~* \.(tpl|db|sqlite|ya?ml|log|md|json|dist)$ { deny all; }   注意 Many FTP clients do not transfer dotfiles (.htaccess) by default. After uploading, always run ./fegg-cli doctor <URL> from your local machine.

searchDocs.title: Routine updates​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli core:status # current version, and whether core files were changed ./fegg-cli core:update --dry-run # show the difference to the latest release (changes nothing) ./fegg-cli core:update # update to the latest tag (vX.Y.Z) ./fegg-cli core:update v5.1.0 # update to a given version npm run build:scss # rebuild the CMS CSS if htdocs/cms/scss changed   The release is fetched with git. If you can clone from GitHub over SSH (git clone git@github.com:... works for you), no token is needed.Only core files are replaced: htdocs/_fegg/core/, htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess and htdocs/cms/. site/, htdocs/index.php, htdocs/.htaccess and fegg-cli are not changed.If core files were edited in the project, the command lists them and stops. Move those changes to overrides in site/ (see Directory structure) and run it again. Add --force only if you really want to overwrite them.The replaced files are kept in htdocs/_fegg/site/data/core-backup/<old version>-<timestamp>/.After the update, the template cache is cleared and fegg-cli migration runs automatically.Finally, the core/UPGRADE.md sections for every version crossed are printed. They list what you have to change by hand (entry files, .htaccess, deprecated APIs). Read them.  Run the tests and check the site, then commit. git status should show only core files.

searchDocs.title: Changing the source repository​
searchDocs.content: By default the release is fetched from git@github.com:lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git. To use another repository (a fork, or HTTPS), set it in the project:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/fegg_update.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; $fegg_update['repository'] = 'https://github.com/lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git';   The environment variable FEGG_UPDATE_REPO takes precedence over this file.

searchDocs.title: When the server has no SSH (FTP-only hosting)​
searchDocs.content: Run ./fegg-cli core:update in your local working copy, then run the tests and check that everything works.Commit the changed files.Upload htdocs/_fegg/core/ and htdocs/cms/ (including the built CSS) over FTP. Upload htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess only if it changed.fegg-cli migration cannot run on the server. For versions that change tables, either upload a database file built locally or open /cms/migrate/ in the CMS.Check the live site with ./fegg-cli doctor https://example.com.

searchDocs.title: Merging upstream with git​
searchDocs.content: You can also update by adding the skeleton repository as upstream and merging a release tag:  git remote add upstream git@github.com:lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git git fetch upstream --tags git merge v5.1.0   If the project only edited site/, there are no conflicts in the core. The skeleton's sample files in site/ (sample controllers and templates) may also have changed; in that case keep the project's version.

searchDocs.title: Versions​
searchDocs.content: Version	MeaningPatch (5.0.x)	Fixes inside the core. core:update alone is enough Minor (5.x.0)	New features. Optional work for projects is described in UPGRADE.md Major (x.0.0)	Changes that require fixes to project code  The full text, including the release procedure for skeleton maintainers, is in docs/updating.md of the skeleton repository.

searchDocs.title: 1. Find the changes the project made to the core​
searchDocs.content: Find the skeleton version the project started from (version in package.json, or @version in fegg/Application.php). Check out the skeleton at that tag, copy the project's core files over it (fegg/, code/lib/, code/application/cms/, code/template/cms/, htdocs/cms/, htdocs/index.php, htdocs/.htaccess) and look at git diff. Keep the list; each item is moved to site/ in step 3.

searchDocs.title: 2. Move files into the new structure​
searchDocs.content: v3 / v4	Fegg 5fegg/*.php, code/lib/ (DB_pdo, LH_FW, Validation, Tool, ...)	htdocs/_fegg/core/ (use the new version) Project values in fegg/settings.php	htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php fegg/MyApplication.php	htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Controller.php code/lib/Modifire.php	htdocs/_fegg/site/functions/modifier.php Other project libraries in code/lib/	htdocs/_fegg/site/src/ (Site\) Shared CMS screens in code/application/cms/ (Index, Login, Logout, Media, Image, Multi, Migrate, Register)	htdocs/_fegg/core/controller/ (use the new version) Everything else in code/application/	htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/ (cms/ becomes Cms/) Shared CMS templates in code/template/cms/	htdocs/_fegg/core/template/cms/ (use the new version) Everything else in code/template/	htdocs/_fegg/site/template/ code/config/, code/config/database/ (project tables)	htdocs/_fegg/site/config/, htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/ code/data/	htdocs/_fegg/site/data/ htdocs/index.php, fegg-cli	Recreate from core/dist/index.php.dist and core/dist/fegg-cli.dist htdocs/.htaccess	Add the Fegg rules from core/dist/htaccess.dist  Then:  Copy htdocs/_fegg/core/, htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess and htdocs/cms/ from the Fegg 5 skeleton, and run npm run build:scss. Recreate the entry files. If the project changed the paths in index.php, set the three constants (FEGG_HTML_DIR, FEGG_CORE_DIR, FEGG_SITE_DIR) to match (see Directory structure). Add the FilesMatch block and the RewriteRule (^|/)_fegg(/|$) - [F,L] line from htaccess.dist to htdocs/.htaccess. Move the project files with git mv (keeps the history). Carry over the changed values of the old fegg/settings.php (developer_ip, run_mode, maintenance_page_url, Basic authentication, languages) to site/config/settings.php. Copy site/config/env.php.dist to site/config/env.php on each development or staging server and set 'FEGG_ENV' => 'development': without it the site runs as production and shows no error details (see Settings). Create site/config/cms_menu.php with one block per post type that was in the old CMS menu. Replace the removed constants until grep -rn "FEGG_DIR\|FEGG_CODE_DIR" htdocs/_fegg/site finds nothing: v3 / v4	Fegg 5FEGG_CODE_DIR . '/config/...'	FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/config/...' FEGG_CODE_DIR . '/data/...'	FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/...' FEGG_CODE_DIR . '/application/...'	FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/controller/...' FEGG_CODE_DIR . '/lib/...'	A namespaced class in site/src/ FEGG_DIR . '/...'	Not needed (autoloaded)  At this point the site should work again. Old-style controllers (no namespace, extends MyApplication, getClass()) still run.

searchDocs.title: 3. Move core changes into overrides in site/​
searchDocs.content: Go through the list from step 1:  Changed template of a shared CMS screen: put the changed file at the same path in site/template/cms/.Changed controller of a shared CMS screen: extend the core class (class Media extends \Fegg\Controller\Cms\Media) and write only the changed methods (see Controller).Code added to MyApplication: move it to __init() of site/controller/Controller.php.Changed shared library: create a subclass in site/src/ and use it.  When ./fegg-cli core:status prints No changes to core files., this step is done.

searchDocs.title: 4. Move to namespaces​
searchDocs.content: The Fegg 4 style keeps working through Fegg\Legacy, but every use writes Fegg deprecated: ... to the PHP error log, and the compatibility layer will be removed in Fegg 6. Use the log to fix the code step by step.  Fegg 4: code/application/cms/News.php <?php class News extends MyApplication { public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_lh = $this->getClass('LH_FW', 'news'); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id')); } }   Fegg 5: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/News.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; class News extends Controller // Site\Controller\Cms\Controller: the CMS base { protected $_cmsSection = 'news'; // replaces new Helper('news') and the isAuth() check public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id')); } public function delete($id) { $this->requirePost(); // deletes are POST forms with the CSRF token // ... } }   CMS screens extend Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (copy site/controller/Cms/Controller.php from the skeleton), not Site\Controller\Controller: it checks the login and the CSRF token of every POST. Delete links in copied CMS list templates become POST forms (see Controller).  v3 / v4	Fegg 5MyApplication	Site\Controller\Controller (public pages), Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (CMS screens) Application / CommandApplication	Fegg\Application / Fegg\CommandApplication Model, ModelWhere, ModelOrder, ...	Fegg\Model, Fegg\Model\Where, Fegg\Model\Order, ... DB_pdo	Fegg\Database\Pdo LH_FW	Fegg\Cms\Helper Validation	Fegg\Validation ReCAPTCHA, Turnstile	Fegg\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA, Fegg\Captcha\Turnstile Tool/Date, Tool/File, Tool/Mail, Tool/OEmbed, Tool/RSS, Tool/Trim, Tool/Upload	Fegg\Tool\Date, Fegg\Tool\File, ... $this->getClass('LH_FW', 'news')	new \Fegg\Cms\Helper('news') $this->getClass('Validation')	new \Fegg\Validation() $this->getClass('Tool/Upload')	new \Fegg\Tool\Upload() $this->getClass('MyLib/Foo')	new \Site\MyLib\Foo() in site/src/MyLib/Foo.php  Inside a namespace, prefix PHP's own classes with \ (new \Exception, new \DateTime, \PDO::PARAM_INT).  You are done when grep -rn "getClass\|MyApplication\|extends Model\b" htdocs/_fegg/site finds nothing and the error log has no Fegg deprecated entries.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour changes to check​
searchDocs.content: Fegg 5 fails loudly where Fegg 4 was silent. The full list is in the 5.0.0 section of htdocs/_fegg/core/UPGRADE.md. The ones most likely to affect an old project:  Database errors throw Fegg\Database\QueryException (the message includes the SQL and its parameters) instead of printing and calling exit. Uncaught, it is a logged HTTP 500.Missing templates, include targets and transclude parents throw Fegg\Template\TemplateException (HTTP 500) instead of printing "Can't Read" into the page. ./fegg-cli template:lint lists them all.Template blocks are checked: an unclosed block or an extra {{ end }} throws with the line number.Sections are passed to the parent template as closures. Code that called the global section_<name>() functions directly must be rewritten.updateWhere(), deleteWhere() and eraseWhere() with an empty condition throw instead of affecting every row. Pass '1 = 1' where every row was really meant.Model::order(), join() and the table / id / visible options accept only plain names. Move expressions to orderRaw().{{ options }} escapes labels and values, and {{ hidden }} escapes values.OR in conditions is put in brackets before the model adds the visible flag and valid = 1. In Fegg 4, where('a = ?', 1)->where('b = ?', 2, 'OR') also returned unpublished and deleted rows matching b; such lists can get shorter.Arrays reach modifiers: {{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }} now prints the joined tags (it printed nothing).where() fragments with OR are bracketed: where('category = ?', 1)->where('a = ? OR b = ?', ...) is category = 1 AND (a = ? OR b = ?). Fegg 4 matched rows of every category.No more exit: displayPage(), redirect(), requirePost() and the CMS login check throw Fegg\Http\Halt. A catch (\Throwable $e) around them must rethrow it (see Controller). Replace your own exit in controllers with $this->halt().Environment: error details need a developer_ip address and FEGG_ENV other than production (site/config/env.php). FEGG_TEST_ENVIRONMENT no longer looks at the host name.Sessions and cookies: a session starts only when something is written to it. setCookie() takes SameSite as its own argument, and unsetCookie() really deletes the cookie (see Parameters).Security headers (X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, nosniff, Referrer-Policy) are sent with every response. A page meant to be framed by another site calls $this->allowFraming() (see Security).CMS login: logout is a POST. Copied CMS frame templates in site/template/cms/ add the class js-cms-logout to the logout link. Run fegg-cli migration for the login throttling table cms_login_attempt. /cms/login/create/... is gone: use fegg-cli user:create (see fegg-cli).Uploads check the content against the extension; add the @content message to a copied site/config/file_error_message.php (see Upload).htdocs/.htaccess: remove the <IfModule mod_php5.c> block and the Apache 2.2 Order / Deny from all lines (500 on Apache 2.4), and add the dotfile rules of core/dist/htaccess.dist. fegg-cli doctor warns about the old lines.Captcha keys and the database DSN move to env.php: the skeleton's database_config.php and contact/contact_config.php read them with feggEnv(). Copied old files keep working; move the keys out of committed files when convenient.Route-only controllers: controllers that implement Fegg\Http\RouteOnly (such as the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page) are only reached through site/config/route.php. Add a route such as $route['about/'] = 'page/render/about'; for each static page that was reached as /page/render/... (see URL).

searchDocs.title: Additional work for v3 projects​
searchDocs.content: Mail (Fegg\Tool\Mail) uses PHPMailer. sendWithFile(), setInputCharset() and setSendCharset() were removed: add attachments with pushAttached() and call send(). A failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception.Trailing slash: URLs without an extension are redirected (301) to the same URL with a trailing /. Check the keys in route.php and the links in templates.PHP 8: fix deprecation warnings in the project code (for example passing null to string functions).

searchDocs.title: 5. Check​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint prints OK php -l reports no syntax errors for the PHP files under htdocs/_fegg (excluding vendor/ and data/) ./fegg-cli migration against a copy of the production database only adds new core tables such as cms_login_attempt (no project table definition is missing) ./fegg-cli core:status prints No changes to core files. Public pages, the contact form (through to sending), CMS login, create / edit / delete for each post type, and media and image uploads work Every post type appears in the CMS side menu and on the dashboard The PHP error log has no warnings and no Fegg deprecated entries After deploying, ./fegg-cli doctor https://<production URL> prints OK and the CMS dashboard shows no protection warnings  To roll back, redeploy the old branch. The table definitions are compatible, so the same database file works before and after the migration.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array ReCAPTCHA::auth( string $response, [ float $threshold = null ] )   Sends the token to https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify and returns an array:  Key	Data type	Remarkssuccess	boolean	true when the API returned success, the score is not below the threshold and there is no error errors	array	Error messages (English for the API error codes; a Japanese message when the score is below the threshold)  When the service cannot be reached or does not answer with HTTP 200 JSON, success is false and errors has one message asking the visitor to try again later. A warning is written to the application log.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$response	string Token posted by the widget (g-recaptcha-response) $threshold	float	null	Minimum score for this call. null: the threshold given to the constructor

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA; $recaptcha = new ReCAPTCHA(feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''), 0.5); $result = $recaptcha->auth($this->in('g-recaptcha-response')); if (!$result['success']) { $errorMessage = implode(',', $result['errors']); }

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import the class and create it with new, passing the secret key. Then pass the posted token to auth().  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA; use Fegg\Captcha\Turnstile; use Fegg\Validation; class Entry extends Controller { public function confirm() { $validation = new Validation(); // reCAPTCHA (the secret comes from site/config/env.php) $recaptcha = new ReCAPTCHA(feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''), 0.5); $result = $recaptcha->auth($this->in('g-recaptcha-response')); if (!$result['success']) { $validation->setError('g-recaptcha-response', implode(',', $result['errors'])); } // Cloudflare Turnstile $turnstile = new Turnstile(feggEnv('FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET', '')); $result = $turnstile->auth($this->in('cf-turnstile-response')); if (!$result['success']) { $validation->setError('cf-turnstile-response', implode(',', $result['errors'])); } } }

searchDocs.title: Keys​
searchDocs.content: The keys differ per server, and the secret keys must not be committed. Put them in site/config/env.php (or environment variables) and read them with feggEnv():  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY' => '...', 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET' => '...', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY' => '...', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET' => '...',   Use different keys (or the providers' test keys) for development and production. On a test server the keys can go in the committed site/config/env/staging.php (see Test servers deployed with git pull):  	Site key	SecretTurnstile, always passes	1x00000000000000000000AA	1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA Turnstile, always fails	2x00000000000000000000AB	2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA  Test secrets accept only the dummy token of the test site keys (Cloudflare); never use them in production. reCAPTCHA v3 has no test keys: register the test server's domain, and set FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SCORE_THRESHOLD to 1.0 to see a rejection. When a captcha is enabled but a key is empty, every form is rejected and an error is logged.

searchDocs.title: Contact form​
searchDocs.content: The contact form of the skeleton supports both. Enable one in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/contact/contact_config.php with $_enable_recaptcha or $_enable_turnstile; the file reads the keys from feggEnv():  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/contact/contact_config.php $_enable_recaptcha = true; $_recaptcha_key = feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY', ''); $_recaptcha_secret = feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''); $_recaptcha_score_threshold = 0.5;   The widgets are output by site/template/template/antispam.tpl, and site/controller/Contact.php verifies them. Projects whose old contact_config.php has the keys written in it keep working; move them to env.php when convenient.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Every library is a namespaced class that is loaded by the autoloader. Import it with use and create it with new.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use Fegg\Validation; class Contact extends Controller { public function post() { $validation = new Validation(); $validation->required('mail', $this->in('mail'), array('@required', 'Email')); if (!$validation->isError()) { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send($this->in('mail'), 'Sender name', 'from@example.com'); } } }   メモ Fegg 4 code such as $this->getClass('Tool/Mail') still works in Fegg 5 through Fegg\Legacy, but every use is written to the PHP error log as Fegg deprecated: ... and it will be removed in Fegg 6. Replace it with new. Fegg 4	Fegg 5$this->getClass('Validation')	new \Fegg\Validation() $this->getClass('Tool/Mail', $subject, $body)	new \Fegg\Tool\Mail($subject, $body) $this->getClass('Tool/Upload')	new \Fegg\Tool\Upload() $this->getClass('ReCAPTCHA', $secret)	new \Fegg\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA($secret) $this->getClass('DB_pdo')	new \Fegg\Database\Pdo() The same applies to the other Tool/... classes (Tool/Date, Tool/File, Tool/OEmbed, Tool/RSS, Tool/Trim), which became Fegg\Tool\Date and so on.

searchDocs.title: Extension Libraries​
searchDocs.content: Library	Class	DescriptionValidation	Fegg\Validation	Providing some functions for validation Database	Fegg\Database\Pdo	Providing necessary functions for using database Model	Fegg\Model	Extended Database Library for LH project File	Fegg\Tool\File	Providing some functions for managing files/directories Upload	Fegg\Tool\Upload	Providing some functions for uploading/validating files Mail	Fegg\Tool\Mail	Providing some functions for sending email (PHPMailer wrapper) RSS	Fegg\Tool\RSS	Providing some functions for analyzing RSS document Trim	Fegg\Tool\Trim	Providing some functions for processing image (especially image crop) Date	Fegg\Tool\Date	Providing some functions for calculating dates OEmbed	Fegg\Tool\OEmbed	Getting the embed URL of a YouTube video etc. through oEmbed Captcha	Fegg\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA, Fegg\Captcha\Turnstile	Verifying Google reCAPTCHA / Cloudflare Turnstile responses

searchDocs.title: Project libraries​
searchDocs.content: Put your own classes in htdocs/_fegg/site/src/ with the Site\ namespace. They are autoloaded in the same way.  htdocs/_fegg/site/src/MyLib/Foo.php <?php namespace Site\MyLib; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Foo { }   Controller use Site\MyLib\Foo; $foo = new Foo();

searchDocs.title: External Libraries​
searchDocs.content: These libraries are bundled in htdocs/_fegg/core/vendor/ and autoloaded.  PHPMailer (7.0) Used by Mail. Namespace PHPMailer\PHPMailerA failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception Spyc YAML document loader (global class Spyc)Used by the database migration (fegg-cli migration)  JSON documents are handled with PHP's own json_encode and json_decode.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); // Raw SQL with ? placeholders $rows = $db->setQuery( 'SELECT category, count(*) AS n FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 GROUP BY category HAVING n > ?', array(1) )->execute()->all(); // Or build the query $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->setOrder('post_date DESC')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();   A query is built with the set* methods and a build method (select, count, insert, update, delete ...), or written with setQuery. execute runs it, then all, one, getAffectedRow or getLastIndexId read the result. After execute() the built query is forgotten, so each query starts clean.

searchDocs.title: Automatic queries​
searchDocs.content: Queries built with the build methods get the automatic parts of database_regular_use_query.php (see Configuration): valid = 1 on SELECT and count, created / modified / valid on INSERT and modified on UPDATE. Queries written with setQuery() get nothing added.

searchDocs.title: Values and placeholders​
searchDocs.content: Values are always bound to ? placeholders. Integers and booleans are bound as integers, null as NULL, everything else as strings (so count(*) > ? works on SQLite).In setWhere, setHaving and setOn, an array bound to one placeholder expands it: id = ? and id IN (?) become id IN (?, ?, ...), <> / != / NOT IN become NOT IN, LIKE ? becomes (... LIKE ? OR ... LIKE ?) and NOT LIKE ? becomes (... NOT LIKE ? AND ...). An empty array matches no row (=, IN, LIKE) or every row (<>, NOT IN, NOT LIKE). An array on any other operator throws InvalidArgumentException.A ? inside a quoted string literal ('?') is not a placeholder.Table, column and ORDER BY text given to the set* methods is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A failed connection or query throws Fegg\Database\QueryException (a RuntimeException). Its message ends with the SQL with its values filled in, for example no such column: nope (SQL: SELECT nope FROM cms_news WHERE title = 'it''s'). getSql() returns the SQL with its ? placeholders and getParameters() the values. Uncaught, it becomes an HTTP 500 and is written to the PHP error log and the application log. Fegg 4 printed the error (to developer IPs only) and called exit instead.  Controller use Fegg\Database\QueryException; try { $db->setQuery($sql, $params)->execute(); } catch (QueryException $e) { // e.g. a duplicate key error_log($e->getMessage()); }

searchDocs.title: Connections and transactions​
searchDocs.content: Connections are opened once per DSN and user name and shared by every Pdo instance and every model.SELECT and PRAGMA queries run on a slave, other queries on the master (see Configuration). masterServer and slaveServer choose the server for the next query.beginTransaction opens a transaction on the master. Until commit or rollBack, every query of every instance and every model runs inside it. Model::transaction does this for you.

searchDocs.title: Database connect setting​
searchDocs.content: The connection is set in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database_config.php. The skeleton's file reads the values from feggEnv() (an environment variable, then site/config/env.php, see Settings), so the file itself is committed and the same on every server. Without any value it uses the SQLite file site/data/db/db.db.  site/config/database_config.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; /** * Database connection settings * * FEGG_DB_DSN PDO DSN. Default: the SQLite file below * FEGG_DB_USER user name (MySQL) * FEGG_DB_PASSWORD password (MySQL) * FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN read-only replica (optional; default: the master) * FEGG_DB_PATH SQLite file path. As an environment variable it wins over FEGG_DB_DSN * in env.php (the test suite uses it) */ $_sqlite_only = getenv('FEGG_DB_PATH') !== false && getenv('FEGG_DB_DSN') === false; if ($_sqlite_only) { $_dsn = 'sqlite:'.getenv('FEGG_DB_PATH'); } else { $_dsn = feggEnv('FEGG_DB_DSN', 'sqlite:'.feggEnv('FEGG_DB_PATH', FEGG_SITE_DIR.'/data/db/db.db')); } // Master database (a single server) $database_config['master'] = array( 'dsn' => $_dsn, 'username' => feggEnv('FEGG_DB_USER', ''), 'password' => feggEnv('FEGG_DB_PASSWORD', ''), ); // Slave databases (multiple servers allowed) $database_config['slave'] = array( array( 'dsn' => $_sqlite_only ? $_dsn : feggEnv('FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN', $_dsn), 'username' => $database_config['master']['username'], 'password' => $database_config['master']['password'], ), );   master is used for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, schema changes and transactions. SELECT and PRAGMA queries use one of the slave entries, picked at random. With a single database, both use the same DSN.dsn, username and password are passed to PHP's PDO.A connection that fails throws Fegg\Database\QueryException instead of printing the error and exiting.new \Fegg\Database\Pdo('name') reads name/database_config.php and name/database_regular_use_query.php instead, for a second database.Projects created before this file used feggEnv() may keep their own database_config.php. Move the passwords out of committed files into env.php when convenient.

searchDocs.title: MySQL​
searchDocs.content: SQLite is the default. For MySQL (5.7 / 8.x) or MariaDB, set the connection in site/config/env.php (or as environment variables):  site/config/env.php 'FEGG_DB_DSN' => 'mysql:host=127.0.0.1;port=3306;dbname=example;charset=utf8mb4', 'FEGG_DB_USER' => 'example', 'FEGG_DB_PASSWORD' => '...',   Always add charset=utf8mb4 to the DSN, or emoji and other 4-byte characters are lost.The connection runs with sql_mode = ANSI_QUOTES: Fegg quotes names with ", so in raw SQL write string literals with single quotes (WHERE title = 'foo', not "foo", which is a column name). Queries are buffered../fegg-cli migration, migration:db2schema and /cms/migrate/ work on MySQL as on SQLite. Tables are created as InnoDB with utf8mb4_unicode_ci, and changed tables are altered in place (ADD / MODIFY / DROP COLUMN).  The YAML types are mapped like this (a size written in the YAML, such as VARCHAR(100), is used as written):  YAML type	MySQL typeINTEGER	INT CHAR	VARCHAR(255) TEXT	MEDIUMTEXT BOOLEAN	TINYINT(1) DATETIME	DATETIME BLOB	LONGBLOB REAL	DOUBLE  The YAML type is kept in the column comment (fegg:CHAR), so migration:db2schema writes the same YAML back. Indexes on TEXT columns use the first 191 characters.  警告 As on SQLite, fegg-cli migration drops every table that is not in a YAML file, and removes columns that are not in the YAML. Give the site a database of its own (never one shared with another application), and check the pending changes on /cms/migrate/ when in doubt: it lists them before the "Run migration" button applies them.  The skeleton's MySQL tests run with composer test:mysql against the server set in FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_DSN, FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_USER and FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD. Each test creates and drops its own database.

searchDocs.title: Automatic append query configuration​
searchDocs.content: The queries added automatically to queries built by Fegg\Model and the build methods of Fegg\Database\Pdo are set in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/database_regular_use_query.php. Do not edit the core: to change them, copy the file to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database_regular_use_query.php (config files are looked up in site/config first, then core/config).  CURRENT_TABLE is replaced with the table name, and now() with the current date and time. An item that the query already sets (for example valid given to insertRow()) is not added again.  core/config/database_regular_use_query.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; /** * Automatically appended queries * * Queries appended automatically when the "select", "insert", "update" and "delete" methods of the DB class run * (to be extended as needed). */ $database_regular_use_query = array( // Queries appended regardless of the table 'regular_use' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'count' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'modified = now(), created = now(), valid = 1', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => "modified = now()", 'where' => '', ), ), /* // Queries appended per table 'table' => array( 'table_name' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'show_flag = 0', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now(), create_datetime = now()', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now()', 'where' => '', ), ), ), */ );   This is why every table used with Fegg\Model needs valid, created and modified columns. To skip these queries, see unsetRegularUseQuery(), unsetRegularUseQueryForTable() and disabledRegularUseQuery() (Model, Pdo).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::all( [ string $index = '' ] )   Returns the rows of the last SELECT or PRAGMA run with execute, as associative arrays. With $index, the rows are keyed by that column.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$index	string	''	Column to use as the array key

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); // -> array(0 => array('news_id' => 1, 'title' => 'A'), 1 => array('news_id' => 2, 'title' => 'B'), ...) $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all('news_id'); // -> array(1 => array('news_id' => 1, 'title' => 'A'), 2 => array('news_id' => 2, 'title' => 'B'), ...)

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::beginTransaction()   Opens a transaction on the master database. Until commit or rollBack, every query of every Pdo instance and every model runs inside it.  Throws LogicException when a transaction is already open. With models, prefer Model::transaction(), which commits, rolls back and handles nesting for you.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); try { $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'B'))->insert('cms_lab')->execute(); $db->commit(); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $db->rollBack(); throw $e; }

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $rename	string New table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Alter Table "sample" RENAME TO "sample_old" $db->alterRenameTo('sample', 'sample_old')->execute();
