searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::close()   Drops the connection this instance used from the shared connections, so the next query (of any instance) opens a new one. The connection of an open transaction is kept. PHP closes connections at the end of the request, so this is rarely needed.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); $db->close();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static void Pdo::closeAll()   Drops every shared connection. An open transaction is rolled back. The next query opens a new connection. Useful in long-running commands and tests.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; Pdo::closeAll();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::commit()   Commits the transaction opened with beginTransaction. Any instance can commit it. Throws LogicException when no transaction is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->commit();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::compile()   Builds the query without running it or forgetting it. Read it with getQuery and getParam, or with the values filled in with getLastQuery.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->setOrder('created desc')->setLimit(10, 20)->select('cms_news')->compile(); echo $db->getQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By created desc Limit 20, 10 print_r($db->getParam()); // -> Array ( [0] => 2 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Pdo::__construct( [ string $env = '' ] )   Loads database_config.php and database_regular_use_query.php (see Configuration). Nothing is connected until the first query; connections are shared by every instance.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$env	string	''	Config sub directory: 'name' reads name/database_config.php and name/database_regular_use_query.php

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); $rows = $db->setQuery('SELECT * FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 AND category = ?', array(2))->execute()->all();

searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::count( string $table )   Builds Select Count(*) as number_of_records From (...) AS "count_temp" around the SELECT that select would build, so conditions, joins and groups are counted correctly. Read the result with one()['number_of_records'].

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::createIndex( string $table, array $field )   Builds Create [UNIQUE] Index "name" ON "table" (columns).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $field	array Index definition (below)

searchDocs.title: Index definition​
searchDocs.content: Key	Data type	Remarksname	string	Index name unique	boolean	Create a UNIQUE index target	string	Columns, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Create UNIQUE Index "sample_title" ON "sample" (title) $db->createIndex('sample', array('name' => 'sample_title', 'unique' => true, 'target' => 'title'))->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::delete( [ string $table = '' ] )   Builds a DELETE on $table with the condition set with setWhere. This removes the rows; for a soft delete (valid = 0) use Model::delete().  Pdo does not refuse a DELETE without a condition: without setWhere() every row is removed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string	''	Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Delete From "cms_news" Where news_id = ? $db->setWhere('news_id = ?', 3)->delete('cms_news')->execute(); $deleted = $db->getAffectedRow();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::dropTable( string $table )   Builds Drop Table "table".

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Drop Table "sample_old" $db->dropTable('sample_old')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::createTable( string $table, array $field )   Builds a Create Table. Tables are normally defined in site/config/database/*.yaml and created with ./fegg-cli migration.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $field	array List of column definitions (below)

searchDocs.title: Column definition​
searchDocs.content: Every key must be present.  Key	Data type	Remarksname	string	Column name type	string	Column type notnull	boolean	Add NOT NULL dflt_value	mixed	Default value (null, '' or 0: no default) pk	boolean	Add PRIMARY KEY ai	boolean	Add AUTOINCREMENT

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Create Table "sample" (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT DEFAULT 'none') $db->createTable('sample', array( array('name' => 'id', 'type' => 'INTEGER', 'notnull' => true, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => true, 'ai' => true), array('name' => 'title', 'type' => 'TEXT', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => 'none', 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), ))->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::dropIndex( string $index )   Builds Drop Index "index".

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$index	string Index name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Drop Index "sample_title" $db->dropIndex('sample_title')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::disabledRegularUseQuery()   Skips every automatic query (for every table and for the table, see Configuration) for every later query of this instance. To skip them for one query only, use unsetRegularUseQuery and unsetRegularUseQueryForTable.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->disabledRegularUseQuery(); // Select * From "cms_news" (also the rows with valid = 0) $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::execute()   Builds the query (when a build method such as select was called) or takes the one set with setQuery, and runs it. SELECT and PRAGMA queries run on a slave and their rows are read with all or one; other queries run on the master. Inside a transaction every query runs on the transaction's connection. Afterwards the query being built is forgotten (see unsetInitQueryFlag).  Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection or the query fails. Its message ends with the SQL with the values filled in.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getLastIndexId()   Returns the ID generated by the last INSERT on the connection (PDO::lastInsertId()), as a string. Call it on the same instance, right after execute.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = (int) $db->getLastIndexId(); // -> 24

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getLastQuery()   Returns the last query run with execute (or built with compile), with the values filled in and quoted. It is for logs and debugging only: never run the result. To get the SQL and the values separately, use getQuery and getParam.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('title = ?', "it's")->select('cms_news')->execute(); echo $db->getLastQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where title = 'it''s' And "cms_news".valid = 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Pdo::getAffectedRow()   Returns the number of rows the last query inserted, updated or deleted. After a SELECT the value depends on the driver (0 on SQLite); count the rows of all instead.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('visible' => 0))->setWhere('category = ?', 3)->update('cms_news')->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow(); // -> 4

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::getLastQueryDebug()   Returns array('query' => ..., 'parameter' => ...): the last query with its ? placeholders, and the values bound to them.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->execute(); print_r($db->getLastQueryDebug());   Output Array ( [query] => Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 [parameter] => Array ( [0] => 2 ) )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getQuery()   Returns the last query built by compile or execute, with its ? placeholders. getParam returns the values.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->compile(); echo $db->getQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::getParam()   Returns the values bound to the ? placeholders of the last query built by compile or execute, in order.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ? AND news_id IN (?)', 2, array(5, 6))->select('cms_news')->compile(); print_r($db->getParam()); // -> Array ( [0] => 2 [1] => 5 [2] => 6 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::id( string $index )   Returns the values of one column of every row of the last SELECT, as a list.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$index	string Column name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $titles = $db->setItem('title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->id('title'); // -> array('A', 'B', 'C')

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::insert( string $table )   Builds an INSERT on $table from the values set with setValues (or setItem). created, modified and valid are added unless given (see Configuration). Run it with execute and read the new ID with getLastIndexId.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "category", modified, created, valid) Values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample', 'category' => 2))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId(); // -> '24'

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool Pdo::inTransaction()   Returns true while a transaction opened with beginTransaction (by any instance, or by Model::transaction()) is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); if (!$db->inTransaction()) { $db->beginTransaction(); }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::masterServer()   Connects to the master database (see Configuration) and runs the next query on it, also when it is a SELECT. Use it to read a row right after writing it when the slaves may lag behind. Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection fails.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int|null Pdo::getReturnCode()   Returns the number of affected rows of the last query that was not a SELECT or PRAGMA (null before the first one). Prefer getAffectedRow. A failed query throws Fegg\Database\QueryException, so there is no error code to check.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $code = $db->getReturnCode(); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId(); // Read it back from the master $row = $db->masterServer()->setWhere('news_id = ?', $id)->select('cms_news')->execute()->one();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array|null Pdo::one()   Returns the first row of the last SELECT or PRAGMA, or null when it returned no row.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $row = $db->setWhere('news_id = ?', 1)->select('cms_news')->execute()->one(); if ($row === null) { // not found }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::pragma( string $table, string $mode )   Builds an SQLite PRAGMA on $table. Read the rows with all after execute. SQLite only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $mode	string Pragma mode (below)

searchDocs.title: Pragma mode​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Querytable	PRAGMA table_info("table") (also any unknown mode) index_list	PRAGMA index_list("table") index	PRAGMA index_info("table")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Columns of cms_news: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk $columns = $db->pragma('cms_news', 'table')->execute()->all(); // Indexes of cms_news: seq, name, unique, origin, partial $indexes = $db->pragma('cms_news', 'index_list')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::reset()   Forgets everything set for the next query (table, items, conditions, joins, order, limit ...), turns the reset after execute back on (see unsetInitQueryFlag) and re-enables the automatic queries unless disabledRegularUseQuery was called. The result and the last query are kept.  execute() already does this after a successful query. A query that throws keeps its state, so call reset() after catching a QueryException when you reuse the instance. Fegg\Model does this by itself.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\QueryException; $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); try { $db->setWhere('no_such_column = ?', 1)->select('cms_news')->execute(); } catch (QueryException $e) { $db->reset(); } $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::rollBack()   Discards every write since beginTransaction. Any instance can roll it back. Throws LogicException when no transaction is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); try { $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->commit(); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $db->rollBack(); throw $e; }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::select( string $table )   Builds a SELECT on $table from what was set with setItem (columns, default *), setJoin / setOn, setWhere, setGroup, setHaving, setOrder and setLimit. CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1 is added (see Configuration). Run it with execute.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC Limit 0, 10 $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2) ->setOrder('post_date DESC') ->setLimit(10) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setGroup( string $query )   Sets GROUP BY. The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Another call appends its text directly, without a comma, so give every column in one call.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Columns, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 Group By category $rows = $db->setItem('category, count(*) AS n')->setGroup('category')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setInitQueryFlag()   Turns the reset after execute back on (the default), after unsetInitQueryFlag.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Count and fetch with the same conditions $db->unsetInitQueryFlag()->setWhere('category = ?', 2); $count = $db->count('cms_news')->execute()->one(); $db->setInitQueryFlag()->setLimit(10); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setIncrement( string $column, int|float $by )   Adds "column" = "column" + ? to an update, so the addition happens in the database and simultaneous requests do not lose counts. Model::increment() uses it.  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $by is not an int or a float.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Numeric column $by	int/float Amount to add; negative to subtract

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Update "cms_news" Set modified = ?, "view_count" = "view_count" + ? Where news_id = ? $db->setIncrement('view_count', 1)->setWhere('news_id = ?', 5)->update('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setHaving( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds to the HAVING clause, used with setGroup. Parameters work as in setWhere: one per placeholder, and an array expands its placeholder.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 Group By category Having count(*) > ? $rows = $db->setItem('category, count(*) AS n') ->setGroup('category') ->setHaving('count(*) > ?', 3) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setItem( string $query, [ array $parameter = '' ] )   Sets the columns of a query.  Without $parameter: the columns of a SELECT ('news_id, title', expressions allowed).With an associative array: the values of an INSERT / UPDATE, matched to the columns in $query by name. A listed column missing from the array is written as ''.With a list: the values in the order of the columns in $query.  For INSERT and UPDATE, prefer setValues: it writes only the given columns, can store NULL and checks the column names.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Columns, separated by commas $parameter	array	''	Values (by name or by position)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select news_id, title From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "category", modified, created, valid) Values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) $db->setItem('title, category', array('title' => 'Sample', 'category' => 2))->insert('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setLimit( int $limit, [ int $offset = 0 ] )   Adds Limit offset, limit to a SELECT.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$limit	int Maximum number of rows $offset	int	0	Number of rows to skip

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Order By post_date DESC Limit 20, 10 (rows 21 to 30) $rows = $db->setOrder('post_date DESC')->setLimit(10, 20)->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setJoin( string|array $table, [ string $type = null ] )   Adds a JOIN. Follow it with setOn for the condition. $table is a table name or array('table', 'alias'); the names are quoted as they are.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string/array Table name, or array('table', 'alias') $type	string	null	'LEFT', 'INNER' or 'RIGHT' (anything else: plain JOIN)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select cms_news.title, f.org_name From "cms_news" LEFT JOIN "cms_file" AS "f" ON f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ? Where "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setItem('cms_news.title, f.org_name') ->setJoin(array('cms_file', 'f'), 'LEFT') ->setOn('f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ?', 1) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setOrder( string $query )   Sets ORDER BY. The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Another call appends its text directly, so give every sort key in one call.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string ORDER BY expression

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Order By post_date DESC, news_id DESC $rows = $db->setOrder('post_date DESC, news_id DESC')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setOn( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds the ON condition of the last setJoin. The first call after setJoin() writes ON; another call appends its text after a space. Parameters work as in setWhere.  Throws LogicException when no join was set before.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... LEFT JOIN "cms_file" ON cms_file.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND cms_file.type = ? ... $rows = $db->setJoin('cms_file', 'LEFT') ->setOn('cms_file.file_id = cms_news.file_id') ->setOn('AND cms_file.type = ?', 'pdf') ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setWhere( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds to the WHERE clause. Give one argument per ? placeholder, after the query.  Another call appends its text after a space: write the AND / OR yourself (setWhere('AND title = ?', $title)).An array bound to one placeholder expands it: id = ? and id IN (?) become id IN (?, ?, ...), <> / != / NOT IN become NOT IN, LIKE ? becomes (... LIKE ? OR ... LIKE ?) and NOT LIKE ? becomes (... NOT LIKE ? AND ...). An empty array matches no row (=, IN, LIKE) or every row (<>, NOT IN, NOT LIKE). An array on any other operator (<, BETWEEN ...) throws InvalidArgumentException.A ? inside a quoted string literal ('?') is not a placeholder.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Where category = ? AND title = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 1) ->setWhere('AND title = ?', 'A') ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all(); // ... Where post_date >= ? AND news_id IN (?, ?, ?) ... $rows = $db->setWhere('post_date >= ? AND news_id IN (?)', '2026-01-01', array(1, 2, 3)) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setValues( array $values )   Sets the values of an INSERT or UPDATE from column => value pairs. Unlike setItem, only the given columns are written and null is stored as NULL. Model::insertRow() and Model::updateRow() use it.  Throws InvalidArgumentException for an empty array, a column name that is not a plain name (letters, digits and _, optionally table.column), or a value that is an array or an object.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$values	array Values (column => value)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "image_id", modified, created, valid) Values ('Sample', NULL, ...) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample', 'image_id' => null))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= ?, modified = ? Where news_id = ? $db->setValues(array('title' => 'New title'))->setWhere('news_id = ?', 1)->update('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::simpleArray( string $keyName, string $valueName )   Returns key => value pairs built from two columns of every row of the last SELECT, for example for <select> options.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$keyName	string Column to use as the key $valueName	string Column to use as the value

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $titles = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->simpleArray('news_id', 'title'); // -> array(1 => 'A', 2 => 'B', 3 => 'C')

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::slaveServer()   Connects to one of the slave databases, picked at random (see Configuration), and runs the next query on it. SELECT and PRAGMA queries already use a slave; this sends another query there. Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection fails.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Same as without slaveServer(): a SELECT already uses a slave $rows = $db->slaveServer()->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setQuery( string $query, [ array $parameter = [] ] )   Sets the SQL to run with execute, as it is.  $parameter is the list of values for the ? placeholders, in order. Arrays are not expanded here (they are in setWhere); write one ? per value.Nothing is added automatically: write valid = 1 yourself.Only queries that start with SELECT or PRAGMA return rows (all, one) and run on a slave. Any other query (including WITH ... SELECT) runs on the master as a statement; read getAffectedRow after it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string SQL with ? placeholders $parameter	array	[]	Values, in placeholder order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setQuery( 'SELECT category, count(*) AS n FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 GROUP BY category HAVING n > ?', array(1) )->execute()->all(); $db->setQuery('UPDATE cms_news SET visible = ? WHERE post_date < ?', array(0, '2020-01-01'))->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::truncate( string $table )   Builds Truncate "table", which removes every row. MySQL only: SQLite has no TRUNCATE (use delete without a condition there).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Truncate "sample_log" $db->truncate('sample_log')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetInitQueryFlag()   Keeps what was set (items, conditions, joins, order, limit ...) after execute, so the next query can reuse it. Model::find() uses it to count and fetch with the same conditions. Turn it back on with setInitQueryFlag, or drop everything with reset.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Count and fetch with the same conditions $db->unsetInitQueryFlag()->setWhere('category = ?', 2); $count = $db->count('cms_news')->execute()->one(); $db->setInitQueryFlag()->setLimit(10); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()   For the next query only, skips the queries configured for the table (the table section of database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration). The queries added for every table still apply.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::update( string $table )   Builds an UPDATE on $table from the values set with setValues (or setItem) and setIncrement, and the condition set with setWhere. modified is added unless given. Run it with execute and read the number of updated rows with getAffectedRow.  Unlike Model::updateRowsWhere(), Pdo does not refuse an UPDATE without a condition: without setWhere() every row is updated.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= ?, modified = ? Where news_id IN (?, ?) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'New title')) ->setWhere('news_id IN (?)', array(1, 2)) ->update('cms_news') ->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow(); // -> 2

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetRegularUseQuery()   For the next query only, skips the queries added for every table (regular_use in database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration): valid = 1 on SELECT and count, created / modified / valid on INSERT and modified on UPDATE.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select * From "cms_news" $db->unsetRegularUseQuery()->select('cms_news')->execute(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 (the next query is back to normal) $db->select('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$dateTime	string Base date and time $interval	int Number of days (negative: before) $format	string	'Y-m-d H:i:s'	date() format of the result

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Date::addMonth( string $dateTime, int $interval, [ string $format = 'Y-m-d H:i:s' ] )   Returns $dateTime plus $interval months, formatted with date() format $format. When the day does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. The time is reset to 00:00:00.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$dateTime	string Base date $interval	int Number of months (negative: before) $format	string	'Y-m-d H:i:s'	date() format of the result

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Date and create it with new.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Date; class Event extends Controller { public function index() { $date = new Date(); $this->page['deadline'] = $date->addDay(date('Y-m-d H:i:s'), 7, 'Y/m/d'); $this->page['last_day'] = $date->getTheLastday(date('Y-m-d')); $this->displayPage('event'); } }

searchDocs.title: Date formats​
searchDocs.content: The $dateTime arguments accept YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS and its shorter forms, with or without the separators (2024, 2024/04, 2024-04-01, 20240401, 2024/4/1 9:30), see Date::makeupDateFormat. Other formats are parsed with strtotime(). Date::addDay, Date::addMinute, Date::addMonth, Date::getTheLastday and Date::getDiff (in days) throw InvalidArgumentException when the value cannot be parsed.

searchDocs.title: Time zone​
searchDocs.content: The time zone of the application is set once at startup, from $settings['timezone'] in site/config/settings.php (default FEGG_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, Asia/Tokyo):  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['timezone'] = 'Europe/Paris';   date(), Fegg\Tool\Date and the template modifier feggDate all use it. No Fegg method changes it afterwards:  Date::getSocialTime uses its $timezone argument for that call only.The controller methods $this->getDatetime($format = 'Y-m-d H:i:s', $timeZone = '') and $this->convertDatetime($date, $fromTimezone, $toTimezone) work on their own DateTime objects. Fegg 4 changed the process-wide time zone in them.convertDatetime() returns '' for a date it cannot read (Fegg 4 returned 1970-01-01 ...).  Controller echo $this->getDatetime('Y-m-d H:i', 'UTC'); // now, in UTC echo $this->convertDatetime('2026-04-01 09:00:00', 'Asia/Tokyo', 'Europe/London'); // 2026-04-01 01:00:00 echo $this->convertDatetime('not a date', 'Asia/Tokyo', 'UTC'); // ''

searchDocs.content: public number Date::getDiff( string $fromDateTime, string $toDateTime, [ boolean $month = false ] )   Returns $toDateTime minus $fromDateTime in days. The result is a decimal number when the times of day differ (12 hours is 0.5). With $month, the difference is counted in calendar months, ignoring the days (2024-01-31 to 2024-02-01 is 1).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fromDateTime	string Start date and time $toDateTime	string End date and time $month	boolean	false	true: in months / false: in days

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Date; $date = new Date(); echo $date->getDiff('2024-04-01', '2024-04-10'); // -> 9 echo $date->getDiff('2024-04-10', '2024-04-01'); // -> -9 echo $date->getDiff('2024-01-31', '2024-03-01', true); // -> 2

searchDocs.content: public string Date::getSocialTime( string $date, [ string $timezone = '' ] )   Returns the time between $date and now in Japanese: N日前, N時間前, N分前 or N秒前 (the largest unit that is 1 or more). Returns an empty string when $date is now.  メモ $timezone is the time zone $date is written in, for this call only. The time zone of the application ($settings['timezone']) is not changed. When it is omitted, the application's time zone is used.

'/data/export'); $file->writeFile(FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/export/list.csv', "id,title\n", 'w'); } }   メモ Most methods do nothing (no error, no return value) when the source file or directory does not exist. Check the result yourself, e.g. with file_exists(), when it matters.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Mail; $mail = new Mail(); $mail->body('Mail body'); // Use a template for the body $mail->body($this->fetchPage('/contact/mail/to_admin'));

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Mail and create it with new. A failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception, so wrap the sending in try / catch.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception; class Contact extends Controller { public function post() { $body = $this->fetchPage('/contact/mail/to_admin'); try { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', $body); $mail->send('admin@example.com', 'Sender name', 'from@example.com'); } catch (Exception $e) { // Failed to send: $e->getMessage() } } }   The contact form of the skeleton (htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Contact.php) is a complete example, including Mail::setDebugFlag to write the emails to a log file instead of sending them.

searchDocs.title: SMTP​
searchDocs.content: To send through an SMTP server instead of sendmail, set $settings['mail'] in site/config/settings.php, and put the password in site/config/env.php (or an environment variable) as FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD. Every Mail object then uses it, the contact form included.  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['mail'] = array( 'transport' => 'smtp', 'host' => 'smtp.example.com', 'port' => 587, 'encryption' => 'tls', 'username' => 'user@example.com', );   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php 'FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD' => '...',   Key	Default	Remarkstransport	'sendmail'	'smtp' to use SMTP host	'localhost'	SMTP server. FEGG_SMTP_HOST in env.php overrides it port	587	Port encryption	'tls'	'tls': STARTTLS. 'ssl': SMTPS (usually port 465). '': none username	''	Login user; without it no authentication is used. FEGG_SMTP_USERNAME in env.php overrides it  The connection times out after 10 seconds. Never write the password in settings.php, which is committed.  メモ The PHPMailer instance is available as $mail->_mailer when you need a setting this wrapper does not cover.

Nothing is written when the file or its directory is not writable. The return value is always true.  Mail::send calls this method with the whole message when the debug flag is enabled.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Mail; $mail = new Mail(); $mail->setDebugFlag(true, FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/log/mail.log'); $mail->log('Contact form posted');

searchDocs.content: public boolean Mail::send( mixed $to, [ string $from_name = null, string $from_ad = null ] )   Sends the email with its attachments and returns true on success. A failed send (including an invalid address) throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception.  When the debug flag is enabled with Mail::setDebugFlag, the email is not sent: the whole message is written to the log file with Mail::log instead.  メモ $from_ad is required in practice: without a valid sender address the send throws. Each call sends only to the addresses given to it, so one Mail object can send the same message to several people in turn. To send one email to several recipients, pass them as an array.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$to	mixed Recipient address, or an array of addresses $from_name	string	null	Sender name $from_ad	string	null	Sender address (also used as the envelope sender)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception; try { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send('mail@example.com', 'John Doe', 'from@example.com'); // Several recipients $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send(array('foo@example.com', 'bar@example.com'), 'John Doe', 'from@example.com'); } catch (Exception $e) { // Failed to send: $e->getMessage() }

searchDocs.content: Type	CastINTEGER	(int) FLOAT	(float) DATE	Y-m-d. A number is read as a Unix timestamp, anything else with strtotime() DATETIME	Y-m-d H:i:s. A number is read as a Unix timestamp, anything else with strtotime()  A DATE / DATETIME string that strtotime() cannot read is stored as 1970-01-01; validate dates before writing them.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; class News extends Controller { public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); } public function index() { $this->page['data'] = $this->_model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->listMax(20) ->current($this->in('p')) ->find(); $this->page['pager'] = $this->_model->getPager(); $this->displayPage('news'); } }

searchDocs.title: Tables​
searchDocs.content: Tables are defined in YAML: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/*.yaml (project) and htdocs/_fegg/core/config/database/*.yaml (CMS core tables). ./fegg-cli migration applies them to the database.  Use ./fegg-cli db:schema to see the tables and columns (./fegg-cli db:schema cms_news for one table, --json for JSON). It reads the YAML files, so no database is needed, and it warns about tables that lack the columns below.

searchDocs.title: Required columns​
searchDocs.content: Every table used with Fegg\Model needs these columns. The model fills them by itself (see core/config/database_regular_use_query.php):  Column	Type	Set byvalid	BOOLEAN	1 on insert, 0 by delete. Reads only return rows with valid = 1 created	DATETIME	insert modified	DATETIME	insert and update

searchDocs.title: Creating a model​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', // table name 'id' => 'news_id', // primary key 'visible' => 'visible', // optional: public flag column 'bind' => array('category' => 'INTEGER', 'post_date' => 'DATETIME'), // casts on write ));   The first argument is $is_admin. With false, reads only return rows whose visible column is 1 (public pages). The CMS uses true to see unpublished rows. See Model::__construct.bind types are INTEGER, FLOAT, DATE and DATETIME (case-insensitive). Any other type throws InvalidArgumentException. See Model::addBindParam.Table and column names (table, id, visible, and the names given to order(), join(), whereIn() and the other helpers) must be plain identifiers: letters, digits and _, optionally table.column (news_id, cms_news.post_date). Anything else throws InvalidArgumentException. Never build names from user input.

searchDocs.title: Reading​
searchDocs.content: Controller $rows = $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->whereLike('title', 'news') // contains; % and _ match literally ->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2, 3)) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->listMax(20)->current($this->in('p')) // page size and page number ->find(); // array of rows (associative arrays) $pager = $model->getPager(); // current_page, last_page, number_of_records ... $rows = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5)->all(); // no paging $row = $model->id($id); // one row by primary key, or null $row = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->one(); // first match, or null $title = $model->where('news_id = ?', $id)->value('title'); // one value, or null $ids = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->column('news_id'); // array(3, 5, ...) $count = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->count(); // int $found = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->exists(); // bool   Method	Returnsfind	One page of rows; getPager has the links all	Every matching row (limit caps it) one / id	The first row, or null value	The first column of the first row, or null column	One column of every row, optionally keyed by another column count	Number of rows (of groups, with group()) exists	true when a row matches toSql	The SELECT all() would run, with the values filled in; runs nothing

searchDocs.title: find() or all()​
searchDocs.content: find() pages: set the page size with listMax and the page with current, then read the links with getPager(). all() does not page; limit caps it. Do not use listMax(9999) to get everything, and do not combine limit() with find() (it throws LogicException).

searchDocs.title: Conditions are reset after every query​
searchDocs.content: where(), order(), select(), limit() and the other chain methods only apply to the next query. After every query (find(), all(), one(), count(), insertRow() ...), failed ones included, the model forgets them, so each query starts clean. Model::reset does the same by hand.  The write methods (updateRowsWhere, deleteWhere ...) take their condition as arguments. Conditions chained with where() are not used by them (and are cleared).

searchDocs.title: Writing​
searchDocs.content: Controller $id = $model->insertRow(array('title' => $title, 'category' => 2, 'content' => null)); $n = $model->updateRow(array('title' => $title), $id); // rows updated $n = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 0), 'category = ?', 3); $ids = $model->insertRows(array($row1, $row2)); // one transaction: all rows or none $n = $model->delete($id); // soft delete: valid = 0 $n = $model->erase($id); // removes the row   insertRow, updateRow and updateRowsWhere write only the given keys; null is stored as NULL. Do not pass created, modified or valid unless you mean to override them.Update and delete methods return the number of affected rows.delete and deleteWhere are soft deletes (valid = 0; reads no longer see the row). erase and eraseWhere remove the row.updateWhere(), deleteWhere(), eraseWhere() and updateRowsWhere() refuse an empty condition. Pass '1 = 1' to really affect every row.The older insert and update still work, but they write '' for every listed column missing from the data and cannot store NULL.transaction runs several writes, of any number of models, all or nothing.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A failed query or connection throws Fegg\Database\QueryException. Its message ends with the SQL and its parameters ((SQL: Select ... Where no_such_column = 'x')); getSql() and getParameters() return them separately. Uncaught, it becomes an HTTP 500 and is written to the PHP error log and the application log. Fegg 4 printed the error and called exit instead.  Catch it only when the page can do something useful, for example with a duplicate key:  Controller try { $model->insertRow($row); } catch (\Fegg\Database\QueryException $e) { // ... }   Wrong use of the builder (an array bound to <, an invalid column name, an update without a condition) throws InvalidArgumentException with a message saying what to do instead.

searchDocs.title: Debugging​
searchDocs.content: toSql returns the SELECT a chain would run, without running it. debug prints the last query. Both fill in the values for reading.  Controller echo $model->where('category = ?', 2)->order('post_date', 'desc')->toSql(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC

searchDocs.title: Raw SQL​
searchDocs.content: For what the model cannot express, use Fegg\Database\Pdo directly. It shares the connection (and an open transaction) with the models. Raw queries get no automatic valid / created / modified handling.

Key	Remarkscurrent_page	Page returned by find() page_min	First page number to show (up to 4 before the current) page_max	Last page number to show (up to 4 after the current) previous_page	Previous page. The page size is set with listMax (default 10) and the page with current. find() counts the matching rows first, so getPager can return the page links afterwards.  To get every row without paging, use all. find() throws LogicException when limit was set.

searchDocs.content: public self Model::having( string $query, [ mixed $data = [], string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds a HAVING condition, used with group. $data works as in where: one value, or an array of values in placeholder order. With having(), count counts the groups that match.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders (never put user input in it) $data	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Categories with more than 5 news // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where ... Group By category Having n > 5 $records = $model ->select('category, count(*) AS n') ->group('category') ->having('n > ?', 5) ->all();

searchDocs.title: Complex HAVING query​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->select('category, count(*) AS n, max(post_date) AS latest')->group('category'); $model->having('n > ?', 5); $model->havingOpen(); $model->having('category = ?', 1); $model->having('latest >= ?', '2026-01-01', 'OR'); $model->havingClose(); // ... Group By category // Having n > 5 AND (category = 1 OR latest >= '2026-01-01') $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$group	string Group column(s)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Select category, count(*) AS n // From "cms_news" // Where ... // Group By category $records = $model->select('category, count(*) AS n')->group('category')->all(); // Number of categories that have news $categories = $model->group('category')->count();

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->select('category, count(*) AS n, max(post_date) AS latest')->group('category'); $model->having('n > ?', 5); $model->havingOpen(); $model->having('category = ?', 1); $model->having('latest >= ?', '2026-01-01', 'OR'); $model->havingClose(); // ... Group By category // Having n > 5 AND (category = 1 OR latest >= '2026-01-01') $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$andOr	string	'AND'	How the bracket joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->select('category, count(*) AS n, max(post_date) AS latest')->group('category'); $model->having('n > ?', 5); $model->havingOpen(); $model->having('category = ?', 1); $model->having('latest >= ?', '2026-01-01', 'OR'); $model->havingClose(); // ... Group By category // Having n > 5 AND (category = 1 OR latest >= '2026-01-01') $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.content: public int Model::increment( string $column, mixed $id, [ int|float $by = 1 ] )   Adds $by to $column of the row whose primary key is $id, in the UPDATE itself ("column" = "column" + ?), and returns the number of updated rows. Simultaneous requests do not lose counts, as they would when reading, adding and writing back.  Like every update, it also sets modified. Call unsetRegularUseQuery first to leave modified alone (for example for a view counter).  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $by is not a number.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Numeric column $id	mixed Target primary ID $by	int/float	1	Amount to add; negative to subtract

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // The table has a view_count INTEGER column $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Update "cms_news" Set "view_count" = "view_count" + 1 Where news_id = 24 $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->increment('view_count', 24); // Subtract 2 (modified is updated) $model->increment('view_count', 24, -2);

A public model ($is_admin = false) also returns null for a row that is not visible, and deleted rows (valid = 0) are never returned. Conditions chained before it with where also apply.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $record = $model->id($this->in('id')); if ($record === null) { // 404 }

searchDocs.content: public string Model::insert( string $item, array $data )   Inserts one row and returns the new ID as a string. For new code, use insertRow: insert() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $data is an associative array (values matched to $item by name) or a list (values in the order of $item). created, modified and valid are filled automatically and bind types are applied.

searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values

searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); // Returns the new ID $insertedId = $model->insert($item, $data); // -> '24'

searchDocs.content: public array Model::insertRows( array $rows )   Inserts each row with insertRow inside one transaction and returns the new IDs in order. When one row fails, none is inserted and the exception is rethrown. Throws InvalidArgumentException when an element of $rows is not an array.

searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $ids = $model->insertRows(array( array('title' => 'First', 'category' => 1), array('title' => 'Second', 'category' => 2), )); // -> array(25, 26)

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int|string Model::insertRow( array $row )   Inserts one row from column => value pairs and returns the new ID (an int for integer keys).  Only the given columns are written; null is stored as NULL.created, modified and valid are filled automatically. Give them only to override them.bind types are applied.Throws InvalidArgumentException for an empty array, a column name that is not a plain name, or a value that is an array or an object. A failed insert (for example a duplicate key) throws Fegg\Database\QueryException.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $id = $model->insertRow(array( 'title' => $this->in('title'), 'category' => 2, 'post_date' => '2026-01-15 10:00:00', 'image_id' => null, )); // -> 24

searchDocs.content: public self Model::join( string|array $table, [ string $type = 'INNER', string $on = null, mixed $data = [] ] )   Joins another table. $table is a table name, or array('table', 'alias'); both must be plain names, or InvalidArgumentException is thrown. $on takes ? placeholders and $data works as in where.  The automatic valid = 1 and visible conditions only apply to the model's own table. Add them to $on for the joined table when you need them.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string/array Table name, or array('table', 'alias') $type	string	'INNER'	'INNER', 'LEFT' or 'RIGHT' (anything else: INNER) $on	string	null	ON condition with ? placeholders $data	mixed	[]	Values for the ON placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Select cms_news.*, f.org_name // From "cms_news" // LEFT JOIN "cms_file" AS "f" ON f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = 1 // Where ... $records = $model ->select('cms_news.*, f.org_name') ->join(array('cms_file', 'f'), 'LEFT', 'f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ?', 1) ->find();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::limit( int $count, [ int $offset = 0 ] )   Adds LIMIT to all, column and toSql; one, value and exists use the offset. count ignores it. find pages with listMax and current instead and throws LogicException when limit() was set.  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $count is under 1 or $offset under 0.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$count	int Maximum number of rows $offset	int	0	Number of rows to skip

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // The 5 newest $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5)->all(); // The next 5 (rows 6 to 10) $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5, 5)->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::order( string $order, [ string $duration = 'ASC' ] )   Adds a column to ORDER BY. Call it again for a second sort key.  $order must be a column name (post_date or cms_news.post_date); anything else, such as 'post_date desc' or an expression, throws InvalidArgumentException. Use orderRaw for expressions.$duration is DESC (case-insensitive) or anything else for ASC, so it is safe to pass a sort direction from the request.order('random') sorts in random order (ORDER BY RANDOM(), an SQLite function).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$order	string Column name, or 'random' $duration	string	'ASC'	'ASC' or 'DESC'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Order By post_date DESC,news_id DESC $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->order('news_id', 'desc')->find(); // 3 random news $records = $model->order('random')->limit(3)->all();

searchDocs.content: public array|null Model::one( [ array $options = [] ] )   Returns the first matching row as an associative array, or null when nothing matches. order decides which row is first; the offset of limit is used.

searchDocs.content: public self Model::listMax( [ int $listMax = 10 ] )   Sets the number of rows per page of find. Without it, find() returns 10 rows. A value under 1 is treated as 1. Only find() uses it: use limit with all instead of a large listMax() to get every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$listMax	int	10	Rows per page

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.content: public self Model::orderRaw( string $expression )   Adds an ORDER BY expression as it is. Use it for what order does not accept: CASE, functions, several keys in one string. The expression is written into the SQL unchanged: never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$expression	string ORDER BY expression

searchDocs.title: Example​

Order By CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC $records = $model->orderRaw('CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC')->find();

searchDocs.content: public array Model::pragma( string $mode )   Runs an SQLite PRAGMA on the model's table and returns its rows. SQLite only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$mode	string Pragma mode

searchDocs.title: Pragma mode​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Querytable	PRAGMA table_info("table") (also any unknown mode) index_list	PRAGMA index_list("table") index	PRAGMA index_info("table")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', )); // PRAGMA table_info("cms_news") $columns = $model->pragma('table'); print_r($columns[0]);   Output Array ( [cid] => 0 [name] => news_id [type] => INTEGER [notnull] => 1 [dflt_value] => [pk] => 1 )

searchDocs.content: public self Model::reset()   Forgets the conditions set with the chain methods: where, having, order, join, group, select, listMax, current and limit. The model does this by itself after every query, failed ones included, so call it only to drop a chain you built but did not run. The table, primary key, visible flag, bind types and the pager are kept.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); $model->where('category = ?', 1)->order('post_date', 'desc'); // Changed our mind: start again $model->reset(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where 1 = 1 And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.content: public string Model::toSql()   Returns the SELECT that all would run with the conditions set so far, with the values filled in, without running it. Like after a query, the conditions are cleared afterwards. The values are quoted for reading only: never run the result.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); echo $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2)) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->limit(5) ->toSql();   Output Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND news_id IN (1, 2) AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC Limit 0, 5

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Model::transaction( callable $callback )   Runs $callback in a transaction and returns what it returns. The transaction is committed when the callback returns and rolled back when it throws; the exception is then rethrown.  The callback receives this model.Every query inside the callback takes part, whatever model (or Fegg\Database\Pdo) runs it.A transaction() call inside another one joins the outer transaction.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$callback	callable Receives this model

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Model; $news = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $labs = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_lab', 'id' => 'lab_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $id = $news->transaction(function (Model $news) use ($labs) { $id = $news->insertRow(array('title' => 'A')); $labs->insertRow(array('title' => 'B')); // another model joins the same transaction return $id; });

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::unsetRegularUseQuery()   For the next query only, skips the queries added for every table (regular_use in database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration): the valid = 1 condition of reads, created / modified / valid on insert and modified on update. disabledRegularUseQuery skips them for good.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); // Include the rows deleted with delete() (valid = 0) $records = $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->all(); // Count a view without changing "modified" (the table has a view_count column) $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->increment('view_count', 1);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()   For the next query only, skips the queries configured for this table (the table section of database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration). The queries added for every table still apply; see unsetRegularUseQuery.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); $records = $model->unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()->all();

searchDocs.content: public int Model::update( string $item, array $data, mixed $id )   Updates the row whose primary key is $id and returns the number of updated rows. For new code, use updateRow: update() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL. modified is set automatically and bind types are applied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values $id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); $updated = $model->update($item, $data, 1); // -> 1

searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateRow( array $row, mixed $id )   Updates the row whose primary key is $id and returns the number of updated rows (0 when there is no such row). Only the given columns are written; null is stored as NULL. modified is set automatically, and bind types are applied.  Throws InvalidArgumentException like insertRow.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value) $id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Only title (and modified) are written; the other columns keep their value // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= 'New title', modified = '2026-11-09 17:40:25' Where news_id = 1 $updated = $model->updateRow(array('title' => 'New title'), 1); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateWhere( string $item, array $data, string $where, mixed $wh_data )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. For new code, use updateRowsWhere: updateWhere() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $wh_data is one value, or an array with one value per placeholder. The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException (Fegg 4 updated every row). Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $wh_data	mixed Values for the placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); $updated = $model->updateWhere($item, $data, 'category = ? AND news_id > ?', array(2, 10));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateRowsWhere( array $row, string $where, [ mixed $params = [] ] )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. Columns are written as in updateRow. $params works as in where: one value, or an array of values in placeholder order (an array on a single IN (?) placeholder expands it).  The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row. Conditions chained with where are not used.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value) $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $params	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Hide every news of category 3 $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 0), 'category = ?', 3); $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('category' => 1), 'news_id IN (?)', array(4, 5, 6)); // Every row $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 1), '1 = 1');

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name $from	mixed Lowest value $to	mixed Highest value $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

Where post_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-01-31 23:59:59' AND ... $records = $model->whereBetween('post_date', '2026-01-01 00:00:00', '2026-01-31 23:59:59')->find();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereClose()   Closes the bracket opened with whereOpen.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::where( string $query, [ mixed $data = [], string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds a condition with ? placeholders. Values are always bound, never written into the SQL. Several calls are joined with AND (or OR with $andOr).  $data is one value, or an array of values in placeholder order. A query without placeholders ('note IS NULL') needs none.An array bound to a single placeholder expands it: id = ? and id IN (?) become id IN (?, ?, ...), id <> ? / id != ? / id NOT IN (?) become NOT IN, title LIKE ? becomes (title LIKE ? OR title LIKE ? ...) and title NOT LIKE ? becomes (title NOT LIKE ? AND ...). An empty array matches no row (=, IN, LIKE) or every row (<>, NOT IN, NOT LIKE). An array on any other operator (<, BETWEEN ...) throws InvalidArgumentException when the query runs.A ? inside a quoted string literal ('?') is not a placeholder.An empty $query ('') adds nothing, which is handy for optional search conditions.  A query with its own OR outside brackets is put in brackets when it is joined to other conditions: where('category = ?', 1)->where('title = ? OR summary = ?', array($q, $q)) is category = 1 AND (title = ? OR summary = ?). Fegg 4 wrote category = 1 AND title = ? OR summary = ?, which matched rows of every category. having works the same way.  The conditions the model adds by itself (the visible flag and valid = 1) are joined with AND after yours. When your conditions have an OR outside brackets, the model puts them in brackets first (Where (a = ? OR b = ?) AND ...), so hidden and deleted rows never match. To group conditions inside your own, use whereOpen and whereClose.  For common cases there are helpers that also check the column name: whereIn, whereNotIn, whereLike, whereNull, whereNotNull and whereBetween.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders (never put user input in it) $data	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $records = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->find(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 ... // Several placeholders: an array in placeholder order $records = $model->where('category = ? AND post_date >= ?', array(2, '2026-01-01'))->find(); // An array on one placeholder: IN (...) $records = $model->where('news_id IN (?)', array(1, 2, 3))->find(); // ... Where news_id IN (1, 2, 3) AND ...

searchDocs.title: Complex WHERE query​

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\OEmbed and create it with new, passing the page URL. The constructor throws an Exception when the URL is not supported or the request fails.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\OEmbed; class Movie extends Controller { public function index() { try { $oembed = new OEmbed('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xxxxxxxxxxx'); $this->page['youtube'] = $oembed->media; } catch (\Exception $e) { $this->page['youtube'] = ''; } $this->displayPage('movie'); } }   Template {{ if $page.youtube }} <iframe width="560" height="315" src="{{ $page.youtube|feggUrl }}" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen class="c-youtube"></iframe> {{ end }}

searchDocs.title: Properties​
searchDocs.content: The result is read through these read-only properties.  Property	Data type	Remarksmedia	string	URL to embed: src of the iframe (video), src of the img (photo) or href of the a (link) type	string	video, photo or link data	array	The whole oEmbed response (title, author_name, thumbnail_url, html ...) service	string	Matched service name in the configuration, e.g. youtube url	string	URL passed to the constructor  Reading any other property throws an Exception.

searchDocs.title: Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The services are defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/oembed_schemes.php. Only YouTube is defined by default.  htdocs/_fegg/core/config/oembed_schemes.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; $oembed_schemes = array(); $oembed_schemes['youtube'] = array( 'endpoint' => 'https://www.youtube.com/oembed', 'schemes' => array( '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/watch.*$|i', '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/v/.*$|i', '|^https?://youtu\\.be/.*$|i', '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/playlist\\?list\\=.*$|i', '|^https?://youtube\\.com/playlist\\?list\\=.*$|i', ), );   endpoint is the oEmbed endpoint of the service and schemes are regular expressions matching the supported URLs. To add a service, copy the file to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/oembed_schemes.php and add an entry there (the file in site/config/ is used instead of the core's one).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public OEmbed::__construct( string $url, [ array $config = array() ] )   Finds the service whose schemes match $url, requests its oEmbed endpoint and reads the embedded HTML. The result is available through the properties.  Throws an Exception when no service matches $url, the service has no endpoint, the request fails, or the response has no iframe, img or a element.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string URL of the page to embed $config	array	array()	Options sent to the endpoint (see below)  Key	Data type	Default	Remarksmaxwidth	int	null	Maximum width of the embed maxheight	int	null	Maximum height of the embed

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\OEmbed; $oembed = new OEmbed('https://youtu.be/xxxxxxxxxxx', array('maxwidth' => 640)); echo $oembed->type; // -> "video" echo $oembed->media; // -> "https://www.youtube.com/embed/xxxxxxxxxxx?feature=oembed" echo $oembed->data['title']; // -> Video title

searchDocs.title: Entry data​
searchDocs.content: Each entry returned by RSS::fetch and RSS::fetchAll is an array with these keys.  Key	Data type	Remarkstitle	string	Title pubDate	string	Date as written in the feed (pubDate, or dc:date for RSS 1.0) datetime	DateTime	pubDate as a DateTime object link	string	Link URL description	string	Description (HTML entities decoded) content	string	content:encoded (HTML entities decoded) author	string	dc:creator category	array	Category names (category, or dc:subject for RSS 1.0) tag	array	Always an empty array (not implemented)  メモ Entries whose title contains PR: (advertisements) are skipped.Atom feeds are not supported: no entry is returned.The feed is loaded with simplexml_load_file() in the constructor. A feed that cannot be loaded is not handled, so check the URL beforehand when it may be unavailable.

searchDocs.title: Other languages​
searchDocs.content: When a language code is passed to the constructor (new Upload('en')), the messages are read from config/en/file_error_message.php (searched in site/config/ first, then core/config/).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Upload and create it with new. Set the upload directory, then call Upload::upload with the name of the input[type="file"].  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Upload; class Entry extends Controller { public function post() { $this->loadConfig('upload_dir'); $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setUploadDir($this->config['upload_dir']['path'] . '/entry'); $upload->setMaxFileSize(5); $upload->setFileType(array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'pdf')); if ($upload->upload('file', uniqid('f_'), 'Attachment')) { $data = $upload->getUploadedData('file'); // $data['name'], $data['org_name'], $data['type'], $data['size'] ... } else { $errors = $upload->getErrorMessage('file'); } } }   $this->loadConfig('upload_dir') reads site/config/upload_dir.php (path and url of htdocs/up_dir) into $this->config['upload_dir']. The CMS screens (Fegg\Controller\Cms\Image, Media, Multi) use this class in the same way.  Error messages are defined in file_error_message.php, see Configuration.

searchDocs.title: What is checked​
searchDocs.content: The extension must be allowed by setFileType. Script extensions (php, phtml, phar, cgi ...) are refused even when listed.The content must match the extension: getimagesize() for images, the finfo MIME type for known types. A mismatch is the error @content.Files are saved under the name you give (uniqid('f_'), ...), never under the visitor's file name. Keep the original name (org_name) in the database only.Directories are created with mode 0755 and files saved with 0644.

searchDocs.title: Protecting the upload directory​
searchDocs.content: When the upload directory is below the document root, setUploadDir writes an .htaccess into it that denies and disables scripts (.php, .phtml, .phar, .cgi ...), so an uploaded file can never run as code. The CMS dashboard also writes htdocs/up_dir/.htaccess when it opens, and the skeleton ships the file.  fegg-cli doctor and the CMS dashboard report a missing htdocs/up_dir/.htaccess (see fegg-cli). Remember it when you upload over FTP: many FTP clients skip dotfiles. On nginx, .htaccess is ignored: deny scripts under the upload URL yourself.  location ~* ^/up_dir/.*\.(php\d?|phtml|phar|pht|cgi|pl|py|sh)$ { deny all; }

searchDocs.title: Sending stored files​
searchDocs.content: The CMS sends stored files (/up_dir/file/<id>/, the media and image screens) with Fegg\Http\Download::sendHeaders(). It sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a valid Cache-Control, and an RFC 6266 Content-Disposition with the original name escaped (an ASCII fallback plus the UTF-8 name). HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript files are always sent as attachments, never shown inline. Use it when your own controller sends a stored file:  Controller use Fegg\Http\Download; Download::sendHeaders(array( 'type' => $file['type'], 'size' => filesize($path), 'org_name' => $file['org_name'], ), false); // false: browser cache only (private); true: public $this->halt(file_get_contents($path));

searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::setFileType( array $type )   Replaces the list of allowed extensions. The extensions are compared in lower case. Returns false when $type is not an array. The default is array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif').  Extensions a web server may run as code (php, php5, phtml, phar, pht, phps, cgi, pl, py, rb, sh, asp, aspx, jsp, shtml, htaccess, htpasswd) are always refused, even when listed here.
